sentences.zh: 起著雍涒灘，盡上章閹茂，凡三年。

translations.literal: Beginning with Zhuyong Tantan, ending with Shangzhang Yanmao, three years in all.
translations.idiomatic: Spanning from the year Zhuyong Tantan through Shangzhang Yanmao—a period of three years.

translations.literal: Illustrious Ancestor Emperor Ming, upper scroll, lower part.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming the Illustrious Ancestor, Part One (conclusion)

sentences.zh: 1春，正月，司馬懿攻新城，旬有六日，拔之，斬孟達。

translations.literal: 1. Spring, first month, Sima Yi attacked Xincheng; in sixteen days he took it and beheaded Meng Da.
translations.idiomatic: 1. In spring, during the first month, Sima Yi besieged Xincheng; within sixteen days he captured it and executed Meng Da.

sentences.zh: 申儀久在魏興，擅承製刻印，多所假授；

translations.literal: Shen Yi had long been in Weixing, usurping authority to engrave seals on imperial orders and granting many unauthorized appointments.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Yi had long served in Weixing, where he had taken it upon himself to cut seals and issue credentials on his own authority, handing out many illicit commissions.

sentences.zh: 懿召而執之，歸于洛陽。

translations.literal: Yi summoned and arrested him, then sent him back to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yi summoned him, placed him under arrest, and sent him back to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 子楙尚太祖女清河公主按據《魏志．諸夏侯曹傳》，夏侯楙為夏侯惇之子，即夏侯淵族子，此處「之」字改為「族」。

translations.literal: son Mao married the Grand Ancestor's daughter Princess Qinghe. According to the Biographies of the Xiahous and Caos in the History of Wei, Xiahou Mao was the son of Xiahou Dun—that is, a clansman-son of Xiahou Yuan; here the character zhi is corrected to zu.
translations.idiomatic: Mao married the Grand Ancestor's daughter Princess Qinghe. Note: According to the Biographies of the Xiahous and Caos in the History of Wei, Xiahou Mao was Xiahou Dun's son and thus Xiahou Yuan's clansman-son; the text emends zhi to zu.

sentences.zh: </ref>，文帝少與之親善，及即位，以為安西將軍，都督關中，鎮長安，使承淵處。

translations.literal: </ref>, from youth Emperor Wen was on intimate terms with him; when he took the throne, he appointed him General Who Stabilizes the West, Superintendent of Guanzhong, stationed at Chang'an, to hold Xiahou Yuan's former post.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Emperor Wen had been close to him; when he came to the throne he made him General Who Stabilizes the West, superintendent of Guanzhong, with his seat at Chang'an, to inherit Xiahou Yuan's command.

sentences.zh: 諸葛亮將入寇，與群下謀之，丞相司馬魏延曰：「聞夏侯楙，主婿也，怯而無謀。

translations.literal: Zhuge Liang was about to invade and consulted his subordinates. Chief Minister's Marshal Wei Yan said: "I have heard that Xiahou Mao, the lord's son-in-law, is timid and devoid of strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Liang was preparing a northern campaign and discussed plans with his staff. Chief Minister's Marshal Wei Yan said, "I hear that Xiahou Mao—the emperor's son-in-law—is timid and short on strategy.

sentences.zh: 今假延精兵五千，負糧五千，直從褒中出，循秦嶺而東，當子午而北，不過十日，可到長安。

translations.literal: Now grant Yan five thousand picked troops and five thousand piculs of grain; march straight out from Baozhong, follow the Qin Mountains eastward, strike north at Ziwu, and in no more than ten days we can reach Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Give me five thousand elite troops and rations for five thousand men. I would march straight from Baozhong, follow the Qin Mountains east, then turn north at Ziwu Pass—in under ten days I could be at Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 楙聞延奄至，必棄城逃走。

translations.literal: When Mao hears that Yan has arrived suddenly, he is sure to abandon the city and flee.
translations.idiomatic: When Mao heard that I had come upon him unawares, he would surely abandon the city and flee.

sentences.zh: 長安中惟御史、京兆太守耳。

translations.literal: In Chang'an there would be only the imperial censor and the Administrator of Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Chang'an would hold nothing but the imperial censor and the Administrator of Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 橫門邸閣與散民之穀，足周食也。

translations.literal: The grain in the storehouses at Heng Gate and among the scattered populace would suffice to feed us for weeks.
translations.idiomatic: The grain in the Heng Gate granaries and among the common people would be enough to supply us for weeks.

sentences.zh: 比東方相合聚，尚二十許日，而公從斜谷來，亦足以達。

translations.literal: By the time the eastern forces could assemble and arrive, there would still be some twenty days left, and when Your Excellency came by the Xie Valley route, that too would be enough to get through.
translations.idiomatic: Before eastern reinforcements could gather and arrive, there would still be some twenty days to spare—and when you came up through the Xie Valley, that would be ample time as well.

sentences.zh: 如此，則一舉而咸陽以西可定矣。

translations.literal: In this way, with one stroke everything west of Xianyang could be settled.
translations.idiomatic: In this way we could secure everything west of Xianyang in a single stroke.

sentences.zh: 」亮以為此危計，不如安從坦道，可以平取隴右，十全必克而無虞，故不用延計。

translations.literal: " Liang regarded this as a risky plan; it was better to advance safely by the level road, take Longyou by steady pressure, achieve a perfect tenfold victory without worry—and so he did not adopt Yan's plan.
translations.idiomatic: " Liang judged this a reckless gamble. Better to take the open road, seize Longyou by steady pressure, and win a sure, complete victory without risk—so he rejected Yan's proposal.

sentences.zh: 亮揚聲由斜谷道取郿。

translations.literal: Liang spread word that he would take Mei by the Xie Valley route.
translations.idiomatic: Liang let it be known that he would take Mei by way of the Xie Valley.

sentences.zh: 使鎮東將軍趙雲，揚武將軍鄧芝為疑軍，據箕谷。

translations.literal: He sent General Who Stabilizes the East Zhao Yun and General Who Displays Martial Might Deng Zhi as a diversionary force to hold Jigu.
translations.idiomatic: He sent General Who Stabilizes the East Zhao Yun and General Who Displays Martial Might Deng Zhi with a diversionary force to hold Jigu Pass.

sentences.zh: 帝遺曹真都督關右諸軍亮身率大軍攻祁山，戎陳整齊，號令明肅。

translations.literal: The Emperor dispatched Cao Zhen as superintendent of all forces west of the Pass. Liang personally led the main army against Qishan; the barbarian ranks were orderly and commands clear and strict.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor dispatched Cao Zhen to command all forces west of the Pass. Liang himself led the main army against Qishan; the ranks were orderly and discipline severe.

sentences.zh: 始，魏以漢昭烈既死，數歲寂然無聞，是以略無備豫；

translations.literal: At first Wei, because Emperor Zhaolie of Han had died and for several years all had been quiet without news, had made scarcely any preparations.
translations.idiomatic: At first Wei, believing that with Emperor Zhaolie's death the realm had lain quiet for years, had made almost no preparations.

sentences.zh: 而卒聞亮出，朝野恐懼。

translations.literal: but then suddenly they heard that Liang had marched forth, and court and countryside were filled with fear.
translations.idiomatic: Then word came that Liang had marched out, and court and countryside alike were stricken with fear.

sentences.zh: 於是天水、南安、安定皆叛應亮，關中響震，朝臣未知計所出。

translations.literal: Thereupon Tianshui, Nan'an, and Anding all rebelled to join Liang; Guanzhong shook with the news, and the court ministers did not know what plan to adopt.
translations.idiomatic: Tianshui, Nan'an, and Anding all rose and went over to Liang; Guanzhong trembled at the news, and the court could not settle on a plan.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「亮阻山為固，今者自來，正合兵書致人之術，破亮必也。

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "Liang relies on mountains for his defense; now that he has come out on his own, this exactly fits the art of war for drawing the enemy in—we are sure to defeat Liang.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Liang has been hiding behind the mountains; now he has come out on his own. That is exactly what the military classics call drawing the enemy in—we shall surely break him.

sentences.zh: 」乃勒兵馬步騎五萬，遣右將軍張郃督之，西拒亮。

translations.literal: " He then mustered fifty thousand infantry and cavalry, sent Right General Zhang He to command them, and had them resist Liang in the west.
translations.idiomatic: " He mustered fifty thousand foot and horse, placed Right General Zhang He in command, and sent them west to meet Liang.

sentences.zh: 丁未，帝行如長安。

translations.literal: On dingwei, the Emperor set out for Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei the emperor marched toward Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 初，越巂太守馬謖才器過人，好論軍計，諸葛亮深加器異。

translations.literal: Earlier, Yuexi Administrator Ma Su's talent exceeded that of ordinary men; he delighted in discussing military plans, and Zhuge Liang greatly favored and distinguished him.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Yuexi Administrator Ma Su had shown unusual ability and loved to discourse on strategy; Zhuge Liang had singled him out for special regard.

sentences.zh: 漢昭烈臨終謂亮曰：「馬謖言過其實，不可大用，君其察之！

translations.literal: On his deathbed Emperor Zhaolie of Han told Liang: "Ma Su's words exceed his substance; he must not be entrusted with great responsibility—be sure to examine this!
translations.idiomatic: On his deathbed Emperor Zhaolie told Liang, "Ma Su's words outrun his deeds; do not give him weighty command—watch him closely!

sentences.zh: 」亮猶謂不然，以謖為參軍，每引見談論，自晝達夜。

translations.literal: " Liang still thought otherwise, made Su a staff officer, and whenever he received him for discussion it lasted from day through night.
translations.idiomatic: " Liang still disagreed, made Su a staff officer, and would summon him for talks that ran from dawn till night.

sentences.zh: 及出軍祁山，亮不用舊將魏延、吳懿等為先鋒，而以謖督諸軍在前，與張郃戰于街亭。

translations.literal: When the army marched out to Qishan, Liang did not use veteran generals Wei Yan, Wu Yi, and the like as vanguard, but put Su in command of the forward forces; he fought Zhang He at Jieting.
translations.idiomatic: When the army marched on Qishan, Liang passed over veteran commanders such as Wei Yan and Wu Yi for the vanguard and put Su in charge of the forward divisions; he met Zhang He at Jieting.

sentences.zh: 謖違亮節度，舉措煩擾，捨水上山，不下據城。

translations.literal: Su disobeyed Liang's orders: his movements were fussy and confused; he abandoned the water and encamped on the hills, refusing to descend and hold the walled town.
translations.idiomatic: Su defied Liang's orders, fussed over every detail, left the waterline to camp on the heights, and would not descend to hold the town.

sentences.zh: 張郃絕其汲道，擊，大破之，士卒離散。

translations.literal: Zhang He cut off his water supply, attacked, and routed him utterly; the soldiers scattered.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang He cut off his water, attacked, and shattered his force; the troops scattered.

sentences.zh: 亮進無所據，乃拔西縣千餘家還漢中。

translations.literal: Liang, with no foothold for advance, then evacuated more than a thousand households of Xixian and returned to Hanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: With no footing for advance, Liang withdrew more than a thousand households from Xixian and retreated to Hanzhong.

sentences.zh: 收謖下獄，殺之。

translations.literal: He arrested Su, threw him in prison, and executed him.
translations.idiomatic: He arrested Su, imprisoned him, and had him executed.

sentences.zh: 亮自臨祭，為之流涕，撫其遺孤，恩若平生。

translations.literal: Liang personally conducted the mourning rites, wept for him, comforted his orphaned children, and treated them with the same kindness as in life.
translations.idiomatic: Liang conducted the mourning in person, wept for him, comforted his orphaned children, and treated them with the same kindness as before.

sentences.zh: 蔣琬謂亮曰：「昔楚殺得臣，文公喜可知也。

translations.literal: Jiang Wan said to Liang: "In olden days when Chu killed Dechen, Duke Wen's joy was easy to imagine.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Wan said to Liang, "When Chu put Dechen to death, Duke Wen of Jin could hardly have been more pleased.

sentences.zh: 天下未定而戮智計之士，豈不惜乎！

translations.literal: With the realm still unsettled, to execute a man of strategy and counsel—is that not a thing to regret!
translations.idiomatic: The realm is still unsettled, and you execute a man of strategy—is that not a loss to mourn?

sentences.zh: 」亮流涕曰：「孫武所以能制勝於天下者，用法明也；

translations.literal: " Liang said through tears: "The reason Sun Wu could prevail over the world was that he applied the law with clarity.
translations.idiomatic: " Liang said through tears, "Sun Wu prevailed because his law was clear.

sentences.zh: 是以揚干亂法，魏絳戮其僕。

translations.literal: Therefore when Yang Gan disturbed the regulations, Wei Jiang executed his servant.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Gan broke discipline, Wei Jiang executed his servant.

sentences.zh: 四海分裂，兵交方始，若復廢法，何用討賊邪！

translations.literal: The four seas are divided and arms have only just been joined—if we abandon the law again, of what use is it to campaign against the enemy!
translations.idiomatic: The realm is split and war has only begun—if we set the law aside, how can we hope to defeat the enemy?

sentences.zh: 謖之未敗也，裨將軍巴西王平連規諫謖，謖不能用；

translations.literal: Before Su's defeat, Lieutenant General Wang Ping of Baxi had repeatedly admonished Su, but Su would not heed him.
translations.idiomatic: Before the defeat, Lieutenant General Wang Ping of Baxi had urged Su again and again, but Su would not listen.

sentences.zh: 及敗，眾盡星散，惟平所領千人鳴鼓自守，張郃疑其有伏兵，不往逼也，於是平徐徐收合諸營遺迸，率將士而還。

translations.literal: When defeat came, the masses scattered like stars; only the thousand men under Ping's command beat drums and held their ground. Zhang He suspected an ambush and did not press them; thereupon Ping slowly gathered the fugitives from the various camps and led the officers and men back.
translations.idiomatic: When defeat came the army scattered; only Ping's thousand men beat drums and held formation. Zhang He suspected an ambush and held back, and Ping was able to gather the stragglers from the camps and lead his men home.

sentences.zh: 亮既誅馬謖及將軍李盛，奪將軍黃襲等兵，平特見崇顯，加拜參軍，統五部兼當營事，進位討寇將軍，封亭侯。

translations.literal: After Liang had executed Ma Su and General Li Sheng and stripped Generals Huang Xi and others of their commands, Ping alone was singled out for honor: he was further appointed staff officer, placed in command of five divisions with charge of camp affairs, promoted to General Who Punishes Bandits, and enfeoffed as a district marquis.
translations.idiomatic: After Liang executed Ma Su and General Li Sheng and stripped Huang Xi and others of command, Ping alone was singled out for honor: he was made staff officer, given command of five divisions and camp duties, promoted to General Who Punishes Bandits, and enfeoffed as a district marquis.

sentences.zh: 亮上疏請自貶三等，漢主以亮為右將軍，行丞相事。

translations.literal: Liang submitted a memorial asking to lower his own rank by three grades; the Han ruler made Liang Right General and Acting Chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: Liang memorialized to demote himself three ranks; the Han ruler named him Right General with authority to act as chancellor.

sentences.zh: 是時趙雲、鄧芝兵亦敗於箕谷，雲斂眾固守，故不大傷，雲亦坐貶為鎮軍將軍。

translations.literal: At this time Zhao Yun's and Deng Zhi's forces were also defeated at Jigu; Yun gathered his troops and held firm, so the losses were not severe, but Yun too was demoted to General Who Stabilizes the Army for his part.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Zhao Yun and Deng Zhi were also beaten at Jigu; Yun rallied his men and held fast, so casualties stayed light, but he too was demoted to General Who Stabilizes the Army.

sentences.zh: 亮問鄧芝曰：「街亭軍退，兵將不復相錄，箕谷軍退，兵將初不相失，何故？

translations.literal: Liang asked Deng Zhi: "When the Jieting army withdrew, officers and men could no longer find one another; when the Jigu army withdrew, officers and men did not lose track of each other from the start—why?
translations.idiomatic: Liang asked Deng Zhi, "At Jieting the retreating troops could not keep formation, yet at Jigu they never lost contact—why?

sentences.zh: 」芝曰：「趙雲身自斷後，軍資什物，略無所棄，兵將無緣相失。

translations.literal: " Zhi said: "Zhao Yun personally covered the rear; military stores and equipment were scarcely abandoned at all, so officers and men had no occasion to lose one another.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhi said, "Zhao Yun covered the rear in person; stores and equipment were scarcely abandoned, so the ranks never broke apart.

sentences.zh: 」雲有軍資餘絹，亮使分賜將士，雲曰：「軍事無利，何為有賜！

translations.literal: " Yun had surplus silk from military stores; Liang had it distributed among the officers and men. Yun said: "The campaign brought no gain—why should there be gifts!
translations.idiomatic: " Yun still held surplus silk from the campaign stores; Liang ordered it distributed among the troops. Yun said, "The campaign brought no gain—why distribute rewards?

sentences.zh: 其物請悉入赤岸庫，須十月為冬賜。

translations.literal: Please put all these goods into the Chibi storehouse and hold them until the tenth month for the winter grant.
translations.idiomatic: Put it all in the Chibi storehouse and issue it in the tenth month as the winter allowance.

sentences.zh: 」亮大善之。

translations.literal: " Liang greatly approved.
translations.idiomatic: " Liang was deeply pleased.

sentences.zh: 或勸亮更發兵者，亮曰：「大軍在祁山、箕谷，皆多於賊，而不破賊，乃為賊所破，此病不在兵少也，在一人耳。

translations.literal: Some urged Liang to launch troops again. Liang said: "The main forces at Qishan and Jigu both outnumbered the enemy, yet we did not defeat the enemy and were instead defeated by them—this ailment lies not in having too few troops but in one man.
translations.idiomatic: Some urged Liang to march again. He said, "At Qishan and Jigu our forces outnumbered the enemy, yet we failed to beat them and were beaten instead—the fault lies not in numbers but in one man.

sentences.zh: 今欲減兵省將，明罰思過，校變通之道於將來；

translations.literal: Now I wish to reduce troops and streamline command, make punishments clear and reflect on faults, and test flexible methods for the future.
translations.idiomatic: I mean to trim the army, clarify discipline, reflect on our errors, and work out better methods for what lies ahead.

sentences.zh: 若不能然者，雖兵多何益！

translations.literal: If we cannot do so, what good are many troops!
translations.idiomatic: If we cannot, more troops will do no good.

sentences.zh: 自今已後，諸有忠慮於國，但勤攻吾之闕，則事可定，賊可死，功可蹺足而待矣。

translations.literal: From now on, all who harbor loyal concern for the state need only press hard upon my shortcomings, and affairs can be settled, the enemy can be destroyed, and merit can be awaited with a lift of the foot.
translations.idiomatic: From now on, whoever is loyal to the state should press hard on my faults; then the cause can be settled, the enemy destroyed, and success won in a single stride.

sentences.zh: 」於是考微勞，甄壯烈，引咎責躬，布所失於境內，厲兵講武，以為後圖，戎士簡練，民忘其敗矣。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he reviewed minor services, distinguished the valiant, took blame upon himself, published his failures throughout the realm, drilled troops and rehearsed arms for future plans; the soldiers were honed, and the people forgot the defeat.
translations.idiomatic: " He then reviewed minor services, honored the brave, took blame on himself, published his failures throughout the realm, drilled the army, and planned ahead; the troops were honed and the people soon forgot the defeat.

sentences.zh: 亮之出祁山也，天水參軍姜維詣亮降。

translations.literal: When Liang marched out to Qishan, Tianshui staff officer Jiang Wei came to Liang and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: When Liang marched on Qishan, Tianshui staff officer Jiang Wei came over to him.

sentences.zh: 亮美維膽智，闢為倉曹掾，使典軍事。

translations.literal: Liang admired Wei's courage and wisdom, appointed him Registrar of the Granary Bureau, and put him in charge of military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Liang admired Wei's courage and wit, made him Registrar of the Granary Bureau, and put him in charge of military affairs.

sentences.zh: 曹真討安定等三郡，皆平。

translations.literal: Cao Zhen campaigned against Anding and the other two commanderies and pacified them all.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Zhen subdued Anding and the other two commanderies and restored order.

sentences.zh: 真以諸葛亮懲於祁山，後必出從陳倉，乃使將軍郝昭等守陳倉，治其城。

translations.literal: Zhen, judging that Zhuge Liang, chastened at Qishan, would next come out by Chencang, sent Generals Hao Zhao and others to hold Chencang and repair its walls.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen expected that Liang, stung by Qishan, would next strike through Chencang; he sent Hao Zhao and others to hold the place and repair its walls.

sentences.zh: 3夏，四月，丁酉，帝還洛陽。

translations.literal: 3. Summer, fourth month, on dingyou, the Emperor returned to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: 3. In summer, the fourth month, on dingyou the emperor returned to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 4帝以燕國徐邈為涼州刺史。

translations.literal: 4. The Emperor appointed Xu Miao of Yan as Inspector of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: 4. The emperor appointed Xu Miao of Yan province Inspector of Liang.

sentences.zh: 邈務農積穀，立學明訓，進善黜惡，與羌、胡從事，不問小過；

translations.literal: Miao devoted himself to farming and storing grain, established schools and clarified instruction, promoted the good and removed the wicked, dealt with the Qiang and Hu, and overlooked minor offenses.
translations.idiomatic: Miao promoted farming and grain reserves, founded schools and clear instruction, advanced the worthy and removed the wicked, worked with the Qiang and Hu, and overlooked petty faults.

sentences.zh: </ref>，使知應死者，乃斬以徇。

translations.literal: </ref>, let them know who deserved death, and only then beheaded the offender as a public warning.
translations.idiomatic: Let the chieftain know who deserved death, and only then executed the offender as a public warning.

sentences.zh: 由是服其威信，州界肅清。

translations.literal: Thereby they submitted to his authority and prestige, and the commandery borders were brought to order.
translations.idiomatic: They submitted to his authority, and the province was brought to order.

sentences.zh: 5五月，大旱。

translations.literal: 5. Fifth month, severe drought.
translations.idiomatic: 5. In the fifth month there was a severe drought.

sentences.zh: 6吳王使鄱陽太守周魴密求山中舊族名帥為北方所聞知者，令譎挑揚州牧曹休。

translations.literal: 6. The King of Wu had Poyang Administrator Zhou Fang secretly seek out old clan leaders of renown in the mountains known to the north, and had them deceive and provoke Yang Province Governor Cao Xiu.
translations.idiomatic: 6. The King of Wu had Poyang Administrator Zhou Fang secretly recruit mountain clan leaders whose names were known in the north, to lure and provoke Yang Province Governor Cao Xiu.

sentences.zh: 魴曰：「民帥小丑，不足杖任，事或漏洩，不能致休。

translations.literal: Fang said: "These civilian chieftains are petty figures, not fit to be relied upon; the affair might leak and fail to draw Xiu.
translations.idiomatic: Fang said, "These local chiefs are small fry—not fit for the task; word might leak and we would fail to draw Xiu out.

sentences.zh: 乞遣親人繼箋以誘休，言被譴懼誅，欲以郡降北，求兵應接。

translations.literal: I beg to send a close kinsman, Ji Jian, to entice Xiu, saying that having been reprimanded and fearing execution, he wishes to surrender the commandery to the north and seeks troops to support him.
translations.idiomatic: Send my kinsman Ji Jian to bait Xiu—say I have been censured and fear death, wish to surrender the commandery to Wei, and need troops to receive me.

sentences.zh: 」吳王許之。

translations.literal: " The King of Wu consented.
translations.idiomatic: " The King of Wu agreed.

sentences.zh: 時頻有郎官詣魴詰問諸事，魴因詣郡門下，下發謝。

translations.literal: At the time palace attendants frequently came to Fang to question him on various matters; Fang therefore went to the commandery gate, sent down a letter of apology.
translations.idiomatic: Court envoys kept coming to question Fang; he went to the commandery gate and issued a letter of apology.

sentences.zh: 休聞之，率步騎十萬向皖以應魴；

translations.literal: When Xiu heard of it, he led one hundred thousand infantry and cavalry toward Wan to answer Fang.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiu heard, he led one hundred thousand foot and horse toward Wan to answer Fang.

sentences.zh: 帝又使司馬懿向江陵，賈逵向東關，三道俱進。

translations.literal: The Emperor also sent Sima Yi toward Jiangling and Jia Kui toward Dong Pass; all three columns advanced together.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also sent Sima Yi toward Jiangling and Jia Kui toward Dong Pass—the three columns advanced together.

sentences.zh: 秋，八月，吳王至皖，以陸遜為大都督，假黃鉞，親執鞭以見之；

translations.literal: Autumn, eighth month, the King of Wu reached Wan, appointed Lu Xun Grand Commander, granted the golden axe, and personally held the whip to receive him.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the eighth month, the King of Wu reached Wan, made Lu Xun supreme commander with the golden axe, and received him in person with whip in hand.

sentences.zh: 以朱桓、全琮為左右督，各督三萬人以擊休。

translations.literal: He made Zhu Huan and Quan Cong left and right commanders, each directing thirty thousand men to strike Xiu.
translations.idiomatic: He made Zhu Huan and Quan Cong left and right commanders, each with thirty thousand men to strike Xiu.

sentences.zh: 休知見欺，而恃其眾，欲遂與吳戰。

translations.literal: Xiu knew he had been deceived, but trusting in his numbers wished to give battle with Wu at once.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu knew he had been tricked, but trusting his numbers he meant to fight Wu anyway.

sentences.zh: 朱桓言於吳王曰：「休本以親戚見任，非智勇名將也。

translations.literal: Zhu Huan said to the King of Wu: "Xiu was entrusted only because of kinship; he is no commander of wisdom and courage.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Huan told the king, "Xiu holds command only through kinship—he is no master of strategy or valor.

sentences.zh: 今戰必敗，敗必走，走當由夾石、掛車。

translations.literal: If we fight now he is sure to be defeated; defeated, he is sure to flee; fleeing, he must go by Jia Rock and Gua Cart.
translations.idiomatic: Fight now and he will lose; lose and he will flee—and his retreat must pass Jia Rock and Gua Cart.

sentences.zh: 此兩道皆險厄，若以萬兵柴路，則彼眾可盡，休可生虜。

translations.literal: Both routes are perilous and narrow; if we block the roads with ten thousand men, his host can be destroyed entirely and Xiu taken alive.
translations.idiomatic: Both passes are narrow and deadly; block them with ten thousand men and we can destroy his army and take Xiu alive.

sentences.zh: 臣請將所部以斷之，若蒙天威，得以休自效，便可乘勝長驅，進取壽春，割有淮南，以規許、洛，此萬世一時，不可失時！

translations.literal: Your servant asks to lead his division to cut them off; if by Heaven's majesty we can present Xiu as a trophy, we may then drive the victory home, advance on Shouchun, carve out Huainan, and aim at Xu and Luoyang—this is a chance of ten thousand generations; it must not be missed!
translations.idiomatic: Let me take my command and seal the passes—if Heaven favors us and we capture Xiu, we can drive on to Shouchun, seize Huainan, and threaten Xu and Luoyang. Such a chance comes once in an age—we must not miss it!

sentences.zh: 」權以問陸遜，遜以為不可，乃止。

translations.literal: " Quan asked Lu Xun; Xun thought it inadvisable, and so he stopped.
translations.idiomatic: " Sun Quan asked Lu Xun, who advised against it, and the plan was dropped.

sentences.zh: 尚書蔣濟上疏曰：「休深入虜地，與權精兵對，而朱然等在上流，乘休後，臣未見其利也。

translations.literal: Minister of the Secretariat Jiang Ji submitted a memorial saying: "Xiu has penetrated deep into enemy territory to face Quan's picked troops, while Zhu Ran and others are upstream to strike him from behind—I do not see the advantage.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Jiang Ji memorialized, "Xiu has marched deep into enemy ground to face Sun Quan's elite, while Zhu Ran and others wait upstream to strike his rear—I see no advantage in this.

sentences.zh: 」前將軍滿寵上疏曰：「曹休雖明果而希用兵，今所從道，背湖旁江，易進難退，此兵之絓地也。

translations.literal: " Forward General Man Chong submitted a memorial saying: "Although Cao Xiu is clear-minded and resolute, he seldom employs arms; the route he now follows, with lake at his back and river at his side, is easy to enter and hard to withdraw—this is what strategists call entangling ground.
translations.idiomatic: " Forward General Man Chong wrote, "Cao Xiu is capable but rarely campaigns; his route runs with a lake behind and a river beside—easy to enter, hard to leave. That is what the classics call entangling ground.

sentences.zh: 若入無強口，寵深為之備！

translations.literal: If he enters without a strong opening, Chong will make deep preparations against him!
translations.idiomatic: If he advances without securing his line of retreat, I shall make every preparation against him!

sentences.zh: 」寵表未報，休與陸遜戰於石亭。

translations.literal: " Before Chong's memorial could be answered, Xiu fought Lu Xun at Shiting.
translations.idiomatic: " Before a reply came, Xiu met Lu Xun at Shiting.

sentences.zh: 遜自為中部，令朱桓、全琮為左右翼，三道俱進，衝休伏兵，因驅走之，追亡逐北，逕至夾石，斬獲萬餘，牛馬騾驢車乘萬兩，軍資器械略盡。

translations.literal: Xun himself took the center, ordered Zhu Huan and Quan Cong as left and right wings; all three columns advanced together, broke Xiu's ambush troops, and drove them in flight; pursuing the defeated northward straight to Jia Rock, they killed and captured more than ten thousand, took ten thousand teams of oxen, horses, mules, and donkeys with their carts, and military stores and equipment were nearly all lost.
translations.idiomatic: Xun held the center with Zhu Huan and Quan Cong on the wings; all three columns struck together, broke Xiu's ambush, and routed him. They pursued to Jia Rock, killing or capturing more than ten thousand men and seizing ten thousand teams of draft animals with wagons; arms and supplies were nearly all lost.

sentences.zh: 初，休表求深入以應周魴，帝命賈逵引兵東與休合。

translations.literal: Earlier, Xiu had memorialized asking to advance deep to answer Zhou Fang; the Emperor ordered Jia Kui to lead troops east to join Xiu.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Xiu had asked leave to advance deep to answer Zhou Fang; the emperor ordered Jia Kui east to join him.

sentences.zh: 逵曰：「賊無東關之備，必並軍於皖，休深入與賊戰，必敗。

translations.literal: Kui said: "The enemy has no guard at Dong Pass; they are sure to mass their forces at Wan. Xiu has gone deep to fight the enemy and is sure to be defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Kui said, "The enemy has left Dong Pass unguarded—they will mass at Wan. Xiu has marched deep to fight them and will surely lose.

sentences.zh: 」乃部署諸將，水陸並進，行二百里，獲吳人，言休戰敗，吳遺兵斷夾石。

translations.literal: " He then deployed the generals; by land and water they advanced together. After marching two hundred li they captured a Wu man who said Xiu had been defeated and Wu had left troops to block Jia Rock.
translations.idiomatic: " He deployed his generals and advanced by land and water. After two hundred li they captured a Wu soldier who reported Xiu's defeat and that Wu had left troops to block Jia Rock.

sentences.zh: 諸將不知所出，或欲待後軍，逵曰：「休兵敗於外，路絕於內，進不能戰，退不得還，安危之機，不及終日。

translations.literal: The generals did not know what course to take; some wished to wait for the rear army. Kui said: "Xiu's army is defeated outside and his routes cut within; he cannot advance to fight nor retreat to return—the hinge of safety and peril will not wait a full day.
translations.idiomatic: The generals were at a loss; some wanted to wait for reinforcements. Kui said, "Xiu is beaten in the field and his retreat is cut—he cannot fight forward or withdraw. The crisis will not wait a day.

sentences.zh: 賊以軍無後繼，故至此，今疾進，出其不意，此所謂先人以奪其心也，賊見吾兵必走。

translations.literal: The enemy came here because they thought our army had no follow-on force; if we press forward swiftly and take them unawares—this is what is called forestalling the enemy to seize his heart—the enemy will flee when they see our troops.
translations.idiomatic: They came because they thought we had no reserves. March hard now and take them unawares—that is seizing the initiative. When they see us they will run.

sentences.zh: 若待後軍，賊已斷險，兵雖多何益！

translations.literal: If we wait for the rear army, the enemy will already have blocked the defiles—of what use are many troops then!
translations.idiomatic: Wait for reinforcements and they will already hold the passes—then numbers will do no good!

sentences.zh: 」乃兼道進軍，多設旗鼓為疑兵。

translations.literal: " He then marched by converging routes, setting up many banners and drums as decoy troops.
translations.idiomatic: " He then marched by parallel routes, raising many banners and drums as a show of force.

sentences.zh: 吳人望見逵軍，驚走，休乃得還。

translations.literal: When Wu men saw Kui's army, they fled in alarm, and Xiu was then able to return.
translations.idiomatic: When the Wu soldiers saw Kui's army they fled in alarm, and Xiu was able to get home.

sentences.zh: 逵據夾石，以兵糧給休，休軍乃振。

translations.literal: Kui held Jia Rock and supplied Xiu with troops and grain; Xiu's army then revived.
translations.idiomatic: Kui held Jia Rock and sent Xiu provisions and reinforcements, and Xiu's army recovered.

sentences.zh: 初，逵與休不善，及休敗，賴逵以免。

translations.literal: Earlier, Kui and Xiu had not been on good terms; when Xiu was defeated, he relied on Kui to escape ruin.
translations.idiomatic: Kui and Xiu had never been close, but when Xiu was beaten he owed his escape to Kui.

sentences.zh: 7九月，乙酉，立皇子穆為繁陽王。

translations.literal: 7. Ninth month, on the day Yiyou, the Emperor established his son Prince Mu as Prince of Fanyang.
translations.idiomatic: 7. In the ninth month, on the day Yiyou, the emperor made his son Prince Mu prince of Fanyang.

sentences.zh: 8長平壯侯曹休上書謝罪，帝以宗室不問。

translations.literal: 8. Cao Xiu, Marquis Zhuang of Changping, submitted a memorial asking forgiveness; the Emperor, because he was of the imperial clan, did not inquire into it.
translations.idiomatic: 8. Cao Xiu, Marquis Zhuang of Changping, submitted a letter of apology; the emperor did not pursue the matter, treating him as kin.

sentences.zh: 休慚憤，疽發於背，庚子，卒。

translations.literal: Xiu, shamed and bitter, developed a carbuncle on his back; on the day Gengzi he died.
translations.idiomatic: Shamed and embittered, Xiu developed a festering sore on his back and died on the day Gengzi.

sentences.zh: 帝以滿寵都督揚州以代之。

translations.literal: The Emperor made Man Chong Governor of Yang Province to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor put Man Chong in charge of Yang Province in his place.

sentences.zh: 9護烏桓校尉田豫擊鮮卑郁築鞬，郁築鞬妻父軻比能救之，以三萬騎圍豫於馬城。

translations.literal: 9. Tian Yu, Colonel Protecting the Wuhuan, attacked the Xianbei chief Yuzhujian; Yuzhujian's wife's father Kebineng came to his rescue with thirty thousand cavalry and besieged Yu at Machecheng.
translations.idiomatic: 9. Tian Yu, Colonel Protecting the Wuhuan, attacked the Xianbei leader Yuzhujian. Yuzhujian's father-in-law Kebineng came to the rescue with thirty thousand horsemen and besieged Yu at Machecheng.

sentences.zh: 上谷太守閻志，柔之弟也，素為鮮卑所信，往解諭之，乃解圍去。

translations.literal: Yan Zhi, Administrator of Shanggu—Rou's younger brother—had long been trusted by the Xianbei; he went to reason with them, and they then lifted the siege and departed.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Zhi, Administrator of Shanggu and Yan Rou's younger brother, was trusted by the Xianbei; he went to persuade them, and they raised the siege and left.

sentences.zh: 10冬，十一月，蘭陵成侯王朗卒。

translations.literal: 10. Winter, eleventh month, Wang Lang, Marquis of Cheng of Lanling, died.
translations.idiomatic: 10. In winter, the eleventh month, Wang Lang, Marquis of Lanling, died.

sentences.zh: 11漢諸葛亮聞曹休敗，魏兵東下，關中虛弱，欲出兵擊魏，群臣多以為疑。

translations.literal: 11. Zhuge Liang of Han heard that Cao Xiu had been defeated, that Wei troops were moving east, and that Guanzhong was weak; he wished to march out and strike Wei, but most of the ministers were doubtful.
translations.idiomatic: 11. Zhuge Liang heard that Cao Xiu had been beaten, that Wei was sending troops east, and that Guanzhong was weak. He wanted to march against Wei, but most of the court was skeptical.

sentences.zh: 亮上言於漢主曰：「先帝深慮以漢、賊不兩立，王業不偏安，故託臣以討賊。

translations.literal: Liang submitted to the Han sovereign, saying: "The late Emperor deeply considered that Han and the rebel could not both stand, that an imperial enterprise could not rest in half a kingdom, and therefore entrusted me with punishing the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Liang wrote the Han emperor: "The late Emperor deeply considered that Han and the rebels cannot both endure, that an empire cannot rest in half a kingdom, and therefore entrusted me with punishing the rebels.

sentences.zh: 以先帝之明，量臣之才，固當知臣伐賊，才弱敵強；

translations.literal: With the late Emperor's clarity and his measure of my talent, he surely knew that in attacking the rebels my ability was weak and the enemy strong;
translations.idiomatic: The late Emperor knew my limits: in attacking the rebels my strength was weak and the enemy's was great;

sentences.zh: 然不伐賊，王業亦亡，惟坐而待亡，孰與伐之！

translations.literal: yet if we do not attack the rebels, the imperial enterprise will perish as well—only sitting and awaiting ruin: which is better, that or attacking!
translations.idiomatic: yet if we do not attack them the enterprise will fail all the same. Is it better to sit and wait for ruin, or to fight?

sentences.zh: 是故託臣而弗疑也。

translations.literal: That is why he entrusted me without doubt.
translations.idiomatic: That is why he entrusted me without hesitation.

sentences.zh: 臣受命之日，寢不安席，食不甘味，思惟北征，宜先入南，故五月渡瀘，深入不毛。

translations.literal: From the day I received his charge I could not rest at ease on my mat nor find flavor in my food. Thinking of a northern expedition, I knew I must first secure the south, and so in the fifth month I crossed the Lu River and penetrated deep into barren lands.
translations.idiomatic: From the day I took up this charge I could not sleep or eat in peace. A northern campaign required securing the south first, so in the fifth month I crossed the Lu River and marched deep into unclaimed wilderness.

sentences.zh: 臣非不自惜也，顧王業不可偏全於蜀都，故冒危難以奉先帝之遺意也，而議者以為非計。

translations.literal: It is not that I did not cherish myself, but I saw that the imperial enterprise could not be wholly preserved at the Shu capital alone, and so I braved danger and hardship to fulfill the late Emperor's intent—yet critics called it poor planning.
translations.idiomatic: I did not fail to value my own life, but the enterprise could not be secured from Chengdu alone, so I braved hardship to carry out the late Emperor's intent—and critics called it folly.

sentences.zh: 今賊適疲於西，又務於東，兵法乘勞，此進趨之時也。

translations.literal: Now the rebels are just exhausted in the west and busy in the east; strategy says to strike when the enemy is weary—this is the time to advance.
translations.idiomatic: Now the enemy is worn down in the west and tied down in the east. Strategy says strike a weary foe—this is the moment to advance.

sentences.zh: 謹陳其事如左：高帝明並日月，謀臣淵深，然涉險被創，危然後安。

translations.literal: I respectfully set forth the matter as follows: Emperor Gao's wisdom rivaled sun and moon, his advisers were deep as abysses—yet he braved peril and took wounds, and only after danger came safety.
translations.idiomatic: I respectfully lay out my case: Emperor Gao's wisdom was matchless and his advisers unmatched in depth, yet he still risked wounds in battle and found safety only through danger.

sentences.zh: 今陛下未及高帝，謀臣不如良、平，而欲以長計取勝，坐定天下，此臣之未解一也。

translations.literal: Today Your Majesty has not reached Gao's level, and your advisers are not the equal of Zhang Liang and Chen Ping—yet you wish to win by long-range planning and settle the realm without rising from your seat. This is what I cannot understand, first point.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has not Gao's gifts, nor advisers like Zhang Liang and Chen Ping, yet you would win by patient strategy and settle the realm without stirring. That is my first puzzle.

sentences.zh: 劉繇、王朗各據州郡，論安言計，動引聖人，群疑滿腹，眾難塞胸，今歲不戰，明年不征，使孫策坐大，遂並江東，此臣之未解二也。

translations.literal: Liu Yao and Wang Lang each held provinces and commanderies, discoursing on security and plotting policy, always citing sages—doubts filled their bellies, objections choked their breasts. No war this year, no campaign next, and Sun Ce grew great and swallowed all east of the river. This is what I cannot understand, second point.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yao and Wang Lang held their provinces, talked endlessly of strategy, cited sages at every turn, and filled their councils with doubt. Year after year without fighting let Sun Ce grow mighty until he held all east of the Yangzi. That is my second puzzle.

sentences.zh: 曹操智計殊絕於人，其用兵也，彷彿孫、吳，然困於南陽，險於烏巢，危於祁連，逼於黎陽，幾敗伯山，殆死潼關，然後偽定一時耳；

translations.literal: Cao Cao's wit and schemes were utterly beyond other men; in employing arms he seemed to follow Sun Wu—yet he was trapped at Nanyang, endangered at Wuchao, imperiled at Qilian, pressed at Liyang, nearly defeated at Bowang, almost died at Tong Pass, and only then pretended to settle the age for a time;
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao's genius was beyond compare; in war he seemed to follow Sun Wu—yet he was trapped at Nanyang, endangered at Wuchao, imperiled at Qilian, pressed at Liyang, nearly defeated at Bowang, nearly killed at Tong Pass, and only then won a temporary hold on power;

sentences.zh: 況臣才弱，而欲以不危而定之，此臣之未解三也。

translations.literal: How much more so I, whose talent is weak, yet who would settle matters without danger—this is what I cannot understand, third point.
translations.idiomatic: How then can I, whose talent is feeble, hope to settle things without risk? That is my third puzzle.

sentences.zh: 曹操五攻昌霸不下，四越巢湖不成，任用李服而李服圖之，委夏侯而夏侯敗亡；

translations.literal: Cao Cao five times attacked Chang Ba without taking him; four times crossed Chao Lake without success; employed Li Fu and Li Fu plotted against him; entrusted Xiahou and Xiahou was defeated and destroyed;
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao attacked Chang Ba five times without success, crossed Chao Lake four times without result, trusted Li Fu who turned on him, and relied on Xiahou who was routed and lost;

sentences.zh: 先帝每稱操為能，猶有此失，況臣駑馭，何能必勝！

translations.literal: The late Emperor always praised Cao as capable, yet even he had such failures—how much more I, a slow driver: how can I be sure of victory!
translations.idiomatic: The late Emperor praised Cao's ability, yet even he suffered such reverses—how can I, slow and weak, guarantee victory?

sentences.zh: 此臣之未解四也。

translations.literal: This is what I cannot understand, fourth point.
translations.idiomatic: That is my fourth puzzle.

sentences.zh: 自臣到漢中，中間期年耳，然喪趙雲、陽群、馬玉、閻芝、丁立、白壽、劉郃、鄧銅等及曲長、屯將七十餘人，突將、無前、賨叟、青羌、散騎、武騎一千餘人，皆數十年之內，糾合四方之精銳，非一州之所有；

translations.literal: Since I reached Hanzhong, barely a full year has passed, yet we have lost Zhao Yun, Yang Qun, Ma Yu, Yan Zhi, Ding Li, Bai Shou, Liu He, Deng Tong, and more than seventy company commanders and garrison captains, and over a thousand crack troops, vanguard men, Cong tribesmen, Qingqiang fighters, and cavalry of the scattered and martial guards—all elite forces gathered from all directions within decades, not possessions of a single province alone;
translations.idiomatic: In barely a year since I reached Hanzhong we have lost Zhao Yun, Yang Qun, Ma Yu, Yan Zhi, Ding Li, Bai Shou, Liu He, Deng Tong, and more than seventy company and garrison leaders, and over a thousand of our best shock troops, vanguard fighters, Cong levies, Qingqiang horsemen, and guard cavalry—elite men gathered from across the realm over decades, not the product of one province alone;

sentences.zh: 若複數年，則損三分之二，當何以圖敵！

translations.literal: If we wait several more years, we will lose two-thirds of them—how then can we plan against the enemy!
translations.idiomatic: Wait a few more years and we will lose two-thirds of them—how then can we face the enemy?

sentences.zh: 此臣之未解五也。

translations.literal: This is what I cannot understand, fifth point.
translations.idiomatic: That is my fifth puzzle.

sentences.zh: 今民窮兵疲，而事不可息，事不可息，則住與行，勞費正等，而不及虛圖之，欲以一州之地與賊支久，此臣之未解六也。

translations.literal: Now the people are exhausted and the troops weary, yet the task cannot rest; if the task cannot rest, then staying and going cost equal toil and expense, yet critics would rather sit idle than act—we would use the lands of one province to wage a protracted war against the rebels. This is what I cannot understand, sixth point.
translations.idiomatic: The people are drained and the army worn, yet the task cannot pause. If it cannot pause, staying put costs as much as marching, yet critics would idly wait while we try to sustain a long war against the enemy from one province alone. That is my sixth puzzle.

sentences.zh: 夫難平者事也，昔先帝敗軍於楚，當此時，曹操拊手，謂天下已定。

translations.literal: Matters are hard to settle. When the late Emperor's army was defeated at Chu, at that time Cao Cao clapped his hands and said the realm was settled.
translations.idiomatic: Success is never assured. When the late Emperor lost at Chu, Cao Cao clapped his hands and said the realm was won.

sentences.zh: 然後先帝東連吳、越，西取巴、蜀，舉兵北征，夏侯授首，此操之失計而漢事將成也。

translations.literal: Then the late Emperor allied east with Wu and Yue, west took Ba and Shu, raised armies and marched north, and Xiahou surrendered his head—this was Cao's miscalculation and the Han cause about to succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Then the late Emperor allied with Wu and Yue in the east, took Ba and Shu in the west, marched north, and Xiahou lost his head—Cao's mistake, and Han's cause nearly fulfilled.

sentences.zh: 然後吳更違盟，關羽毀敗，秭歸蹉跌，曹丕稱帝。

translations.literal: Then Wu again broke the alliance, Guan Yu was destroyed in defeat, setback at Zigui, and Cao Pi declared himself emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Then Wu broke faith again, Guan Yu was destroyed, we stumbled at Zigui, and Cao Pi declared himself emperor.

sentences.zh: 凡事如是，難可逆見。

translations.literal: In all matters it is thus—outcomes are hard to foresee.
translations.idiomatic: All affairs are like this—outcomes cannot be foreseen.

sentences.zh: 臣鞠躬盡力，死而後已，至於成敗利鈍，非臣之明所能逆睹也。

translations.literal: Your servant bends body and exhausts strength, until death only then stopping; as for success or failure, profit or harm—that is not what your servant's clarity can foresee.
translations.idiomatic: I will bend every effort until death; success or failure lies beyond what I can foretell.

sentences.zh: 十二月，亮引兵出散關，圍陳倉，陳倉已有備，亮不能克。

translations.literal: Twelfth month, Liang led troops out through San Pass, besieged Chencang; Chencang was already prepared, and Liang could not take it.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Liang marched through San Pass and besieged Chencang, but the city was ready and he could not take it.

sentences.zh: 亮使郝昭鄉人靳詳於城外遙說昭，昭於樓上應之曰：「魏家科法，卿所練也；

translations.literal: Liang sent Hao Zhao's fellow townsman Jin Xin to remonstrate with Zhao from afar outside the walls; Zhao answered from the tower, saying: "The laws and regulations of Wei are what you have practiced;
translations.idiomatic: Liang sent Hao Zhao's fellow townsman Jin Xin to reason with him from outside the walls. Zhao answered from the tower: "You know Wei's military code;

sentences.zh: 我之為人，卿所知也。

translations.literal: what sort of man I am, you know.
translations.idiomatic: you know what sort of man I am.

sentences.zh: 我受國恩多而門戶重，卿無可言者，但有必死耳。

translations.literal: I have received much grace from the state and my family carries heavy obligations—there is nothing you can say to me; I have only death to offer.
translations.idiomatic: I owe the state much and my family stands high—I have nothing to hear from you, only death to give.

sentences.zh: 卿還謝諸葛，便可攻也。

translations.literal: Go back and thank Zhuge for me—you may attack whenever you like.
translations.idiomatic: Go back and tell Zhuge he may attack whenever he likes.

sentences.zh: 」詳以昭語告亮，亮又使詳重說昭，言「人兵不敵，〔無為〕空自破滅<ref>〔無為〕空自破滅據章校及《魏志．明帝紀》注引《魏略》補。

translations.literal: " Xin reported Zhao's words to Liang; Liang sent Xin again to remonstrate with Zhao, saying "Your men cannot match ours, [would achieve nothing] and would destroy yourselves in vain<ref>[Would achieve nothing] and destroy yourselves in vain supplied according to Zhang's collation and the note to the Annals of Mingdi in the History of Wei citing the Brief Account of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Xin told Liang what Zhao had said; Liang sent him again to urge Zhao, saying, "You are outmatched—[do not] destroy yourselves in vain<ref>Supplied according to Zhang's collation and the note to the Annals of Mingdi in the History of Wei citing the Brief Account of Wei.

sentences.zh: </ref>。

translations.literal: </ref>.
translations.idiomatic: End of editorial note.

sentences.zh: 」昭謂詳曰：「前言已定矣，我識卿耳，箭不識也。

translations.literal: " Zhao said to Xin: "What I said before is settled. I know you—but my arrows do not know you.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao told Xin, "My mind is made up. I know you—but my arrows do not."

sentences.zh: 」詳乃去。

translations.literal: " Xin then departed.
translations.idiomatic: Xin withdrew.

sentences.zh: 亮自以有眾數萬，而昭兵才千餘人，又度東救未能便到，乃進兵攻昭，起雲梯衝車以臨城。

translations.literal: Liang, reckoning himself to have tens of thousands of men while Zhao had barely a thousand, and judging that eastern relief could not arrive quickly, advanced to attack Zhao, raising cloud ladders and battering rams to press the walls.
translations.idiomatic: Liang thought he had tens of thousands against Zhao's thousand-odd men, and that eastern relief could not arrive in time, so he pressed the attack with cloud ladders and battering rams.

sentences.zh: 昭於是以火箭逆射其梯，梯燃，梯上人皆燒死；

translations.literal: Zhao then shot fire arrows against the ladders; the ladders caught fire and the men on them were all burned to death;
translations.idiomatic: Zhao fired flaming arrows at the ladders; they caught fire and the men on them burned to death;

sentences.zh: 昭又以繩連石磨壓其衝車，衝車折。

translations.literal: Zhao also used ropes to link millstones and crush the battering rams, and the rams broke.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao also dropped millstones on ropes to smash the battering rams.

sentences.zh: 亮乃更為井闌百尺以射城中，以土丸填塹，欲直攀城，昭又於內築重牆。

translations.literal: Liang then built hundred-foot siege towers to shoot into the city, filled the moat with earth balls, and wished to climb straight up the walls; Zhao again built inner walls within the city.
translations.idiomatic: Liang built hundred-foot siege towers to shoot into the city, filled the moat with earth, and tried to scale the walls directly; Zhao built inner walls within the city.

sentences.zh: 亮又為地突，欲踴出於城裡，昭又於城內穿地橫截之。

translations.literal: Liang also dug underground tunnels, intending to burst out inside the city; Zhao again dug cross-tunnels inside the walls to block them.
translations.idiomatic: Liang dug tunnels to burst into the city; Zhao dug counter-tunnels to cut them off.

sentences.zh: 晝夜相攻拒二十餘日。

translations.literal: Day and night they attacked and resisted each other for more than twenty days.
translations.idiomatic: For more than twenty days they fought day and night.

sentences.zh: 曹真遣將軍費耀等救之。

translations.literal: Cao Zhen sent Generals Fei Yao and others to rescue them.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Zhen sent General Fei Yao and others to the rescue.

sentences.zh: 帝召張郃于方城，使擊亮。

translations.literal: The Emperor summoned Zhang He at Fangcheng and ordered him to strike Liang.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned Zhang He at Fangcheng and ordered him to attack Liang.

sentences.zh: 帝自幸河南城，置酒送郃，問郃曰：「遲將軍到，亮得無已得陳倉乎？

translations.literal: The Emperor personally went to Henancheng, set out wine to send He off, and asked He: "If the general arrives late, will Liang not already have taken Chencang?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor went in person to Henancheng, held a farewell feast for He, and asked: "If you arrive late, will Liang already have taken Chencang?

sentences.zh: 」郃知亮深入無谷，屈指計曰：「比臣到，亮已走矣。

translations.literal: " He, knowing Liang had penetrated deep with no grain, counted on his fingers and said: "By the time I arrive, Liang will already have withdrawn.
translations.idiomatic: He, knowing Liang had marched deep with no supplies, counted on his fingers and said, "By the time I arrive Liang will already have gone.

sentences.zh: 」郃晨夜進道，未至，亮糧盡，引去。

translations.literal: " He pressed forward day and night; before he arrived, Liang's grain was exhausted and he withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: He marched day and night, but before he arrived Liang's supplies ran out and he withdrew.

sentences.zh: 將軍王雙追之，亮擊斬雙。

translations.literal: General Wang Shuang pursued him; Liang struck and beheaded Shuang.
translations.idiomatic: General Wang Shuang pursued him; Liang attacked and killed Shuang.

sentences.zh: 詔賜郝昭爵關內侯。

translations.literal: An edict conferred on Hao Zhao the rank of Marquis within the Passes.
translations.idiomatic: An edict made Hao Zhao Marquis within the Passes.

sentences.zh: 12初，公孫康卒，子晃、淵等皆幼，官屬立其弟恭。

translations.literal: 12. Earlier, Gongsun Kang died; his sons Huang and Yuan and the others were all young, and the officials established his younger brother Gong.
translations.idiomatic: 12. Earlier Gongsun Kang died; his sons Huang and Yuan were still young, and his officials made his younger brother Gong ruler.

sentences.zh: 恭劣弱，不能治國，淵既長，脅奪恭位，上書言狀。

translations.literal: Gong was inferior and weak and could not govern the state; when Yuan had grown, he coerced Gong and seized his position, then submitted a memorial stating the facts.
translations.idiomatic: Gong was weak and could not rule; when Yuan came of age he forced Gong aside, seized power, and reported the matter to the court.

sentences.zh: 侍中劉曄曰：「公孫氏漢時所用，遂世官相承，水則由海，陸則阻山，外連胡夷，絕遠難制。

translations.literal: Attendant-in-Ordinary Liu Ye said: "The Gongsun clan was employed in Han times and has held hereditary office in succession; by water they reach the sea, by land mountains block the way, and outward they connect with barbarians—remote and hard to control.
translations.idiomatic: Attendant Liu Ye said, "The Gongsuns have held hereditary office since Han times; by sea they reach the ocean, by land mountains block the way, and they border barbarian lands—remote and hard to control.

sentences.zh: 而世權日久，今若不誅，後必生患。

translations.literal: Their power has lasted through generations; if they are not punished now, trouble will surely arise later.
translations.idiomatic: Their power has lasted generations; if we do not act now, trouble will follow.

sentences.zh: 若懷貳阻兵，然後致誅，於事為難。

translations.literal: If they harbor disloyalty and block the army, and only then we move to punish them, the matter will be difficult.
translations.idiomatic: Wait until they turn disloyal and raise troops, and punishment becomes far harder.

sentences.zh: 不如因其新立，有黨有仇，先其不意，以兵臨之，開設賞募，可不勞師而定也。

translations.literal: Better to take advantage of their new establishment, when they have factions and enemies, strike before they expect it, bring troops against them, and offer rewards and bounties—then the realm can be settled without weary campaigning.
translations.idiomatic: Better strike while the regime is new and factions and grudges still divide them—surprise them with troops and offer rewards, and the region can be settled without a long campaign.

sentences.zh: 」帝不從，拜淵揚烈將軍、遼東太守。

translations.literal: " The Emperor did not follow this advice and appointed Yuan General Who Displays Martial Might and Administrator of Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor refused and made Yuan General Who Displays Martial Might and Administrator of Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 13吳王以揚州牧呂範為大司馬，印綬未下而卒。

translations.literal: 13. The King of Wu appointed Lu Fan, Governor of Yang Province, as Grand Marshal, but before the seal and cord arrived he died.
translations.idiomatic: 13. Sun Quan appointed Lu Fan, Governor of Yang Province, Grand Marshal, but Fan died before the seal arrived.

sentences.zh: 初，孫策使範典財計，時吳王年少，私從有求，範必關白，不敢專許，當時以此見望。

translations.literal: Earlier, Sun Ce had Fan manage finances; at the time the King of Wu was young and made private requests, but Fan always reported them and did not dare grant them on his own authority—at the time he was respected for this.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Sun Ce had put Fan in charge of finances. Sun Quan was then young and often made private requests; Fan always reported them and never granted them on his own, and was respected for it.

sentences.zh: 吳王守陽羨長，有所私用，策或料覆，功曹周谷輒為傅著簿書，使無譴問，王臨時悅之。

translations.literal: When the King of Wu was magistrate of Yangxian he made some private expenditures; if Ce audited the accounts, Chief Clerk Zhou Gu would falsify the ledger books so there would be no censure—and the King was pleased at the time.
translations.idiomatic: When Sun Quan was magistrate of Yangxian he spent public funds privately; if Sun Ce audited the books, Chief Clerk Zhou Gu falsified the ledgers to avoid trouble, and Sun Quan was pleased at the time.

sentences.zh: 及後統事，以範忠誠，厚見信任，以谷能欺更簿書，不用也。

translations.literal: Later, when he took control of affairs, he deeply trusted Fan for his loyalty, but because Gu could deceive by altering ledger books, he was not employed.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when he took power, he trusted Fan deeply for his loyalty but dismissed Gu for his talent at falsifying accounts.

translations.literal: </ref>, Guo Huai, Inspector of Yong Province, led troops to rescue them.
translations.idiomatic: [End editorial note.] Guo Huai, Inspector of Yong Province, marched to the rescue.

sentences.zh: 亮自出建威，淮退，亮遂拔二郡以歸；

translations.literal: Liang personally came out to Jianwei; Huai withdrew, and Liang then captured the two commanderies and returned;
translations.idiomatic: Liang marched out to Jianwei in person; Huai withdrew, and Liang took both commanderies and returned;

sentences.zh: 漢主復策拜亮為丞相。

translations.literal: the Han sovereign again issued a decree appointing Liang Chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: the Han emperor again appointed Liang chancellor by decree.

sentences.zh: 2夏，四月，丙申，吳王即皇帝位，大赦，改元黃龍。

translations.literal: 2. Summer, fourth month, on the day Bingshen, the King of Wu assumed the imperial throne, proclaimed a general amnesty, and changed the era name to Huanglong.
translations.idiomatic: 2. In summer, the fourth month, on the day Bingshen, Sun Quan declared himself emperor, proclaimed a general amnesty, and changed the era name to Huanglong.

sentences.zh: 百官畢會，吳主歸功周瑜。

translations.literal: All the officials assembled; the Lord of Wu attributed the achievement to Zhou Yu.
translations.idiomatic: All officials assembled, and Sun Quan credited Zhou Yu with the achievement.

sentences.zh: 綏遠將軍張昭舉笏欲褒贊功德，未及言，吳主曰：「如張公之計，今已乞食矣。

translations.literal: General Who Pacifies the Distance Zhang Zhao raised his tablet intending to praise and commend his merit, but before he could speak the Lord of Wu said: "By Master Zhang's plan, we would now be begging for food.
translations.idiomatic: General Zhang Zhao raised his tablet to praise Sun Quan's merit, but before he could speak Sun Quan said, "By your plan, Master Zhang, we would now be begging for food.

sentences.zh: 」昭大慚，伏地流汗。

translations.literal: " Zhao was deeply ashamed and prostrated himself, sweating.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao was deeply ashamed and prostrated himself, drenched in sweat.

sentences.zh: 吳主追尊父堅為武烈皇帝，〔廟號始祖〕<ref>〔廟號始祖〕據《吳志．孫堅傳》注引《吳錄》補。

translations.literal: The Lord of Wu posthumously honored his father Jian as Emperor Wulie, [temple name Shizu]<ref>[Temple name Shizu] supplied according to the note to the Biography of Sun Jian in the History of Wu citing the Records of Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan posthumously honored his father Sun Jian as Emperor Wulie, [temple name Shizu]<ref>[Temple name Shizu] supplied according to the note to the Biography of Sun Jian in the History of Wu citing the Records of Wu.

sentences.zh: </ref>；

translations.literal: </ref>;
translations.idiomatic: End of editorial note;

sentences.zh: 兄策為長沙桓王，立子登為皇太子，封長沙桓王子紹為吳侯。

translations.literal: his elder brother Ce as Prince Huan of Changsha; established his son Deng as crown prince; and enfeoffed Ce's son Shao as Marquis of Wu.
translations.idiomatic: honored his elder brother Sun Ce as Prince Huan of Changsha, made his son Sun Deng crown prince, and enfeoffed Sun Ce's son Shao as Marquis of Wu.

sentences.zh: 以諸葛恪為太子左輔，張休為右弼，顧譚為輔正、陳表為翼正都尉，而謝景、范慎、羊衜等皆為賓客，於是東宮號為多士。

translations.literal: He made Zhuge Ke Left Assistant to the Crown Prince, Zhang Xiu Right Assistant, Gu Tan Assistant Rectifier and Chen Biao Wing Rectifier Commandant, while Xie Jing, Fan Shen, Yang Tong, and others all became guests of the heir—thereafter the Eastern Palace was called rich in talent.
translations.idiomatic: He made Zhuge Ke left assistant to the crown prince, Zhang Xiu right assistant, Gu Tan assistant rectifier and Chen Biao wing rectifier commandant, while Xie Jing, Fan Shen, Yang Tong, and others served as guests of the heir, and the Eastern Palace was said to abound in talent.

sentences.zh: 太子使侍中胡綜作《賓友目》曰：「英才卓越，超逾倫匹，則諸葛恪；

translations.literal: The crown prince had Attendant-in-Ordinary Hu Zong compose the Catalogue of Guests and Friends, saying: "For outstanding talent surpassing all peers, there is Zhuge Ke;
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince had Attendant Hu Zong compose a Catalogue of Guests and Friends, saying: "For outstanding talent surpassing all peers, there is Zhuge Ke;

sentences.zh: 精識時機，達幽究微，則顧譚；

translations.literal: for keen insight into the times and mastery of hidden depths, there is Gu Tan;
translations.idiomatic: for keen insight into the times and mastery of hidden depths, there is Gu Tan;

sentences.zh: 凝辯宏達，言能釋結，則謝景；

translations.literal: for concentrated eloquence, broad understanding, and speech that resolves knots, there is Xie Jing;
translations.idiomatic: for concentrated eloquence, broad understanding, and speech that resolves knots, there is Xie Jing;

sentences.zh: 究學甄微，游夏同科，則范慎。

translations.literal: for exhaustive study and refined discernment, equal to Ziyou and Zixia, there is Fan Shen.
translations.idiomatic: for exhaustive study and refined discernment, equal to Ziyou and Zixia, there is Fan Shen.

sentences.zh: 」羊衜私駁綜曰：「元遜才而疏，子嘿精而很，叔發辯而浮，孝敬深而狹。

translations.literal: " Yang Tong privately rebutted Zong, saying: "Yuansun is talented but careless; Zimo is keen but harsh; Shufa is eloquent but shallow; Xiaojing is deep but narrow.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Tong privately rebutted Zong: "Yuansun is talented but careless; Zimo is keen but harsh; Shufa is eloquent but shallow; Xiaojing is deep but narrow.

sentences.zh: 」衜卒以此言為恪等所惡，其後四人皆敗，如衜所言。

translations.literal: " Tong was ultimately hated by Ke and the others for these words; afterward all four men fell from grace, just as Tong had said.
translations.idiomatic: Tong was hated by Ke and the others for this; afterward all four fell from grace, just as he had predicted.

sentences.zh: 吳主使以並尊二帝之議往告于漢。

translations.literal: The Lord of Wu sent envoys to report to Han the proposal of honoring both emperors equally.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan sent envoys to Han with the proposal that both states honor each other as imperial equals.

sentences.zh: 漢人以為交之無益而名體弗順，宜顯明正義，絕其盟好。

translations.literal: The people of Han thought alliance brought no benefit and the ritual order was not preserved; they held that righteousness should be made clear and the alliance broken.
translations.idiomatic: Han officials thought alliance brought no gain and the ritual order was violated; they argued that righteousness should be declared and the alliance severed.

sentences.zh: 丞相亮曰：「權有僭逆之心久矣，國家所以略其釁情者，求掎角之援也。

translations.literal: Chancellor Liang said: "Quan has harbored rebellious intent for a long time; the reason the state has overlooked his offense is to seek mutual support like pincers.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Zhuge Liang said, "Sun Quan has long harbored rebellious intent; we overlook his offense only to gain an ally who can strike from another angle.

sentences.zh: 今若加顯絕，仇我必深，更當移兵東戍，與之角力，須併其土，乃議中原。

translations.literal: If we now openly break with him, his enmity toward us will surely deepen; we would have to shift troops east to garrison and wrestle with him, and only after merging his lands could we discuss the Central Plains.
translations.idiomatic: Break openly with him now and his hatred will deepen; we would have to shift troops east to fight him, and only after conquering his lands could we turn to the Central Plains.

sentences.zh: 彼賢才尚多，將相輯穆，未可一朝定也。

translations.literal: They still have many talented men, and their generals and ministers are harmonious—it cannot be settled in a single stroke.
translations.idiomatic: They still have many able men, and their generals and ministers work in harmony—it cannot be settled quickly.

sentences.zh: 頓兵相守，坐而須老，使北賊得計，非算之上者。

translations.literal: To halt the army in stalemate, sit and wait until old age, and let the northern enemy profit—this is not the highest strategy.
translations.idiomatic: To halt our armies in stalemate and grow old waiting while the northern enemy profits is no wise strategy.

sentences.zh: 昔孝文卑辭匈奴，先帝伏與吳盟，皆應權通變，深思遠益，非若匹夫之忿者也。

translations.literal: Formerly Emperor Xiaowen spoke humbly to the Xiongnu, and the late Emperor bowed to alliance with Wu—both responded to circumstances with flexible change, thinking deeply of distant benefit, not like the rage of common men.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen once spoke humbly to the Xiongnu, and the late Emperor bowed to alliance with Wu—both adapted to circumstance for long-term gain, not from petty anger.

sentences.zh: 今議者咸以權利在鼎足，不能並力，且志望已滿，無上岸之情，推此，皆似是而非也。

translations.literal: Now critics all say that with profit and power fixed in a tripod of three legs they cannot combine strength, and that Quan's ambition is already fulfilled with no wish to cross to the northern shore—push this reasoning, and it all seems right yet is wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Critics say that with power divided three ways Sun Quan cannot combine strength with us, and that his ambition is already fulfilled with no wish to cross north—push that reasoning and it sounds plausible but is wrong.

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: How so?
translations.idiomatic: How so?

sentences.zh: 其智力不侔，故限江自保。

translations.literal: Their intelligence and strength do not match, therefore they restrict themselves to defending south of the river.
translations.idiomatic: Their wit and strength do not match ours, so they hold to the south of the river for self-preservation.

sentences.zh: 權之不能越江，猶魏賊之不能渡漢，非力有餘，而利不取也。

translations.literal: Quan's inability to cross the river is like the Wei rebels' inability to cross the Han—it is not that strength is surplus, but that advantage does not warrant taking it.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan's inability to cross the Yangzi is like the Wei enemy's inability to cross the Han—not because their strength is surplus, but because the advantage does not warrant the move.

sentences.zh: 若大軍致討，彼高當分裂其地以為後規，下當略民廣境，示武於內，非端坐者也。

translations.literal: If a great army marched to punish them, their leaders would split the territory for future plans, and the lower ranks would raid the people to expand borders and display martial prowess at home—they would not sit idle.
translations.idiomatic: If a great army marched against them, their leaders would carve up territory for future advantage and their subordinates would raid the people to expand their borders and show martial prowess at home—they would not sit idle.

sentences.zh: 若就其不動而睦於我，我之北伐，無東顧憂，河南之眾不得盡西，此之為利，亦已深矣。

translations.literal: If we accept their inaction and treat them as friendly, when we march north we need not worry about looking east; the masses of Henan could not all go west—the advantage in this is already profound.
translations.idiomatic: If we accept their restraint and treat them as allies, our northern campaigns need fear no threat from the east, and the armies of Henan could not all be sent west—the gain would already be great.

sentences.zh: 權僭逆之罪，未宜明也。

translations.literal: Quan's crime of usurpation and rebellion should not yet be made explicit.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan's crime of usurpation and rebellion should not yet be proclaimed openly.

sentences.zh: 」乃遣衛尉陳震使於吳，賀稱尊號。

translations.literal: " So (the court) sent Minister of Guard Chen Zhen as envoy to Wu to congratulate (Sun Quan) on his imperial title.
translations.idiomatic: " The court then sent Chen Zhen, Minister of Guard, as envoy to Wu to congratulate Sun Quan on his imperial title.

sentences.zh: 吳主與漢人盟，約中分天下，以豫、青、徐、幽屬吳，兗、冀、并、涼屬漢，其司州之土，以函谷關為界。

translations.literal: The King of Wu allied with Han, agreeing to divide the realm in half: Yu, Qing, Xu, and You to Wu; Yan, Ji, Bing, and Liang to Han; the lands of Sizhou to be bounded by Hangu Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan allied with Han, agreeing to divide the realm: Yu, Qing, Xu, and You would belong to Wu; Yan, Ji, Bing, and Liang to Han; and the territory of Sizhou would be bounded by Hangu Pass.

sentences.zh: 張昭以老病上還官位及所統領，更拜輔吳將軍，班亞三司，改封婁侯，食邑萬戶。

translations.literal: Zhang Zhao, citing old age and illness, submitted the return of his office and command; he was reappointed General Who Assists Wu, ranked just below the Three Excellencies, re-enfeoffed as Marquis of Lou with a fief of ten thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhao, pleading old age and illness, returned his office and command; he was reappointed General Who Assists Wu, ranked just below the Three Excellencies, re-enfeoffed as Marquis of Lou with a fief of ten thousand households.

sentences.zh: 昭每朝見，辭氣壯厲，義形於色，曾以直言逆旨，中不進見。

translations.literal: Whenever Zhao attended court his words were forceful and his righteous indignation showed on his face; once, speaking bluntly against the imperial will, he was for a time not admitted to audience.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Zhang Zhao attended court his speech was forceful and righteous indignation showed on his face; once, after blunt words against the imperial will, he was for a time barred from audience.

sentences.zh: 後漢使來，稱漢德美，而群臣莫能屈，吳主嘆曰：「使張公在坐，彼不折則廢，安復自誇乎！

translations.literal: Later when a Han envoy came praising Han's virtue, none of the ministers could refute him. The King of Wu sighed: "If Elder Zhang were seated here, they would either be refuted or silenced—how could they boast again!
translations.idiomatic: Later a Han envoy came praising Han's virtue, and none of the ministers could refute him. Sun Quan sighed: "If Elder Zhang were here, they would either be refuted or silenced—how could they boast again!

sentences.zh: 」明日，遣中使勞問，因請見昭，昭避席謝，吳主跪止之。

translations.literal: " The next day he sent a palace messenger to visit Zhao with consolation and asked to see him. Zhao left his seat to apologize; the King of Wu knelt to stop him.
translations.idiomatic: " The next day he sent a palace messenger to console him and asked to see Zhang Zhao. Zhao left his seat to apologize; Sun Quan knelt to stop him.

sentences.zh: 昭坐定，仰曰：「昔太后、桓王不以老臣屬陛下，而以陛下屬老臣，是以思盡臣節以報厚恩，而意慮淺短，違逆盛旨。

translations.literal: Once seated, Zhao looked up and said: "Formerly the Queen Dowager and King Huan did not entrust me to Your Majesty, but entrusted Your Majesty to me—therefore I mean to exhaust my loyalty to repay this great kindness; yet my thoughts are shallow and short, and I have violated Your Majesty's august intent.
translations.idiomatic: Once seated, Zhang Zhao looked up and said: "Formerly the Queen Dowager and King Huan did not entrust me to Your Majesty, but entrusted Your Majesty to me—therefore I mean to exhaust my loyalty to repay this great kindness; yet my thoughts are shallow, and I have violated Your Majesty's august intent.

sentences.zh: 然臣愚心所以事國，志在忠益畢命而已；

translations.literal: Yet the foolish heart with which I serve the state aims only at loyal benefit unto death;
translations.idiomatic: Yet the heart with which I serve the state aims only at loyal service unto death;

sentences.zh: 若乃變心易慮以偷榮取容，此臣所不能也！

translations.literal: If I were to change my heart and alter my purpose to steal glory and win favor—that is what I cannot do!
translations.idiomatic: If I were to change my heart and alter my purpose to steal glory and win favor—that I cannot do!

sentences.zh: 」吳主辭謝焉。

translations.literal: " The King of Wu apologized to him.
translations.idiomatic: " Sun Quan apologized to him.

sentences.zh: 3元城哀王禮卒。

translations.literal: 3. Prince Ai of Yuancheng, Li, died.
translations.idiomatic: 3. Prince Ai of Yuancheng, Li, died.

sentences.zh: 4六月，癸卯，繁陽王穆卒。

translations.literal: 4. In the sixth month, on the day Guimao, Prince Mu of Fanyang died.
translations.idiomatic: 4. In the sixth month, on the day Guimao, Prince Mu of Fanyang died.

sentences.zh: 5戊申，追尊高祖大長秋曰高皇帝，夫人吳氏曰高皇后。

translations.literal: 5. On the day Wushen, (the Emperor) posthumously honored Grand Director of Palace Attendants the High Ancestor as Emperor Gao, and Lady Wu as Empress Gao.
translations.idiomatic: 5. On the day Wushen, the Emperor posthumously honored Grand Director of Palace Attendants the High Ancestor as Emperor Gao, and Lady Wu as Empress Gao.

sentences.zh: 6秋，七月，詔曰：「禮，王后無嗣，擇建支子以繼大宗，則當纂正統而奉公義，何得復顧私親哉！

translations.literal: 6. In autumn, the seventh month, an edict said: "By ritual, when a queen has no heir, a collateral son is chosen to continue the major line—then one ought to succeed the orthodox succession and uphold public duty; how can one again attend to private kinship!
