sentences.zh: 漢宣繼昭帝後，加悼考以皇號；

translations.literal: Emperor Xuan of Han succeeded after Emperor Zhao and added the posthumous title of Emperor to his father Zhao;
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuan of Han succeeded after Emperor Zhao and added the posthumous title of Emperor to his father, the late Zhao;

sentences.zh: 哀帝以外籓援立，而董宏等稱引亡秦，惑誤時期，既尊恭皇，立廟京都，又宏籓妾，使比長信，敘昭穆於前殿，並四位於東宮，僭差無度，人神弗祐，而非罪師丹忠正之諫，用致丁、傅焚如之禍。

translations.literal: Emperor Ai was raised from an outer fief, and Dong Hong and the like cited the fallen Qin, misleading the age; they honored the Respectful Emperor, established a temple in the capital, and also promoted a fief concubine to rank with Changxin, arranging zhao and mu in the front hall and placing four seats in the Eastern Palace—usurpation beyond measure, unblessed by gods and men; yet they did not blame Shi Dan's loyal and upright remonstrance, and thus brought the disaster of Ding and Fu burning like tinder.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ai was raised from an outer fief, and Dong Hong and his allies cited the fallen Qin and misled the age; they honored the Respectful Emperor, built a temple in the capital, and promoted a fief concubine to rank with the Empress Dowager of Changxin, arranging ancestral order in the front hall and placing four seats in the Eastern Palace—usurpation beyond measure, unblessed by gods and men; yet they blamed not Shi Dan's loyal remonstrance, and thus brought the disaster in which the Ding and Fu clans burned like tinder.

sentences.zh: 自是之後，相踵行之。

translations.literal: From then on, one after another carried this out.
translations.idiomatic: From then on, rulers one after another did the same.

sentences.zh: 昔魯文逆祀，罪由夏父；

translations.literal: Formerly Duke Wen of Lu violated ritual sacrifice—the fault lay with Xia Fu;
translations.idiomatic: Formerly Duke Wen of Lu violated ritual sacrifice—the fault lay with Xia Fu;

sentences.zh: 宋國非度，譏在華元。

translations.literal: Song's improper measures—criticism fell on Hua Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: Song's improper measures drew censure upon Hua Yuan.

sentences.zh: 其令公卿有司，深以前世行事為戒，後嗣萬一有由諸侯入奉大統，則當明為人後之義；

translations.literal: Let the ministers and officials take past conduct as a deep warning; if a successor should ever enter from among the feudal lords to receive the great succession, then the meaning of becoming someone's heir ought to be made clear;
translations.idiomatic: Let the ministers and officials take past conduct as a deep warning; if a successor should ever enter from among the feudal lords to receive the great succession, then the meaning of becoming someone's heir ought to be made clear;

sentences.zh: 敢為佞邪導諛時君，妄建非正之號以干正統，謂考為皇，稱妣為後，則股肱大臣誅之無赦。

translations.literal: Whoever dares to be sycophantic and flatter the ruler of the time, rashly establishing illegitimate titles to impinge on the orthodox succession—calling one's father 'emperor' and one's mother 'empress'—the chief ministers shall execute them without pardon.
translations.idiomatic: Whoever dares to be sycophantic and flatter the ruler of the time, rashly establishing illegitimate titles to impinge on the orthodox succession—calling one's father 'emperor' and one's mother 'empress'—the chief ministers shall execute them without pardon.

sentences.zh: 其書之金策，藏之宗廟，著于令典！

translations.literal: Let this be written on a golden covenant, stored in the ancestral temple, and recorded in the statutes!
translations.idiomatic: Let this be written on a golden covenant, stored in the ancestral temple, and recorded in the statutes!

sentences.zh: 7九月，吳主遷都建業，皆因故府，不復增改，留太子登及尚書九官於武昌，使上大將軍陸遜輔太子，並掌荊州及豫章二郡事，董督軍國。

translations.literal: 7. In the ninth month, the King of Wu moved the capital to Jianye; all used the former offices without further additions or changes. He left Crown Prince Deng and the nine directors of the Masters of Writing at Wuchang, appointing Grand General Lu Xun to assist the Crown Prince and jointly manage the two commanderies of Jing and Yuzhang, supervising military and state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: 7. In the ninth month, Sun Quan moved the capital to Jianye, using the former offices without further additions or changes. He left Crown Prince Deng and the nine directors of the Masters of Writing at Wuchang, appointing Grand General Lu Xun to assist the Crown Prince and jointly manage Jing and Yuzhang, supervising military and state affairs.

sentences.zh: 南陽劉廙嘗著《先刑後禮論》，同郡謝景稱之於遜，遜呵景曰：「禮之長於刑久矣；

translations.literal: Liu Yi of Nanyang once wrote "On Punishment Before Ritual"; Xie Jing of the same commandery praised it to Lu Xun. Lu Xun rebuked Jing, saying: "Ritual has long surpassed punishment;
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yi of Nanyang once wrote "On Punishment Before Ritual"; Xie Jing of the same commandery praised it to Lu Xun. Lu Xun rebuked Jing, saying: "Ritual has long surpassed punishment;

sentences.zh: 廙以細辯而詭先聖之教，君今侍東宮，宜遵仁義以彰德音，若彼之談，不須講也！

translations.literal: Yi uses petty argument to distort the teaching of the former sages. You now attend the Eastern Palace and ought to follow benevolence and righteousness to manifest virtuous instruction—talk like his need not be discussed!
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yi uses petty argument to distort the teaching of the sages. You now attend the Eastern Palace and ought to follow benevolence and righteousness to manifest virtuous instruction—talk like his need not be discussed!

sentences.zh: 太子與西陵都督步騭書，求見啟誨，騭於是條於時事業在荊州界者及諸僚吏行能以報之，因上疏獎勸曰：「臣聞人君不親小事，使百官有司各任其職，故舜命九賢，則無所用心，不下廟堂而天下治也。

translations.literal: The Crown Prince wrote to Bu Zhi, Grand Administrator of Xiling, asking to meet him for instruction and guidance. Bu Zhi thereupon listed current affairs within Jing province and the conduct and ability of the various officials and staff to report to him, and submitted a memorial of encouragement, saying: "I have heard that a ruler does not personally attend to small matters but lets the hundred officials and functionaries each perform their duties—thus when Shun appointed the nine worthies, he had no need to apply his mind; without leaving the ancestral hall, the realm was governed.
translations.idiomatic: The Crown Prince wrote to Bu Zhi, Grand Administrator of Xiling, asking to meet him for instruction. Bu Zhi thereupon listed current affairs within Jing province and the conduct and ability of the various officials and staff to report to him, and submitted a memorial of encouragement, saying: "I have heard that a ruler does not personally attend to small matters but lets the hundred officials and functionaries each perform their duties—thus when Shun appointed the nine worthies, he had no need to apply his mind; without leaving the ancestral hall, the realm was governed.

sentences.zh: 故賢人所在，折衝萬里，信國家之利器，崇替之所由也。

translations.literal: Therefore where worthy men are stationed, they repel the enemy a thousand li away—truly the sharp weapon of the state, the source of rise and fall.
translations.idiomatic: Where worthy men are stationed, they repel the enemy a thousand li away—they are truly the sharp weapon of the state, the source of rise and fall.

sentences.zh: 願明太子重以經意，則天下幸甚！

translations.literal: I wish that the enlightened Crown Prince would greatly weigh these principles—then the realm would be greatly blessed!
translations.idiomatic: I wish that the enlightened Crown Prince would greatly weigh these principles—then the realm would be greatly blessed!

sentences.zh: 張紘還吳迎家，道病卒。

translations.literal: Zhang Hong returned to Wu to fetch his family; he fell ill on the road and died.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Hong was returning to Wu to fetch his family when he fell ill on the road and died.

sentences.zh: 臨困，授子〔靖〕留箋曰<ref>授子〔靖〕留箋曰據章注及《吳志．張紘傳》補。

translations.idiomatic: On his deathbed he left his son Jing a note saying<ref>Supplied according to Zhang's commentary and the Biography of Zhang Hong in the History of Wu.

translations.literal: </ref>: "Since ancient times those who had a state or a family all wished to cultivate virtuous government to match a flourishing age; yet when it came to their governance, most lacked fragrance—not because they lacked loyal ministers and worthy assistants, but because the ruler could not overcome his passions and would not employ them.
translations.idiomatic: [End editorial note.] "Since ancient times every ruler of state or clan has wished to cultivate virtue to match a golden age; yet most found their rule lacked luster—not from want of loyal ministers, but because the ruler could not master his passions and would not heed them.

sentences.zh: 夫人情憚難而趨易，好同而惡異，與治道相反。

translations.literal: Now human nature fears difficulty and seeks ease, likes agreement and hates difference—opposite to the way of governance.
translations.idiomatic: Human nature fears difficulty and seeks ease, likes agreement and hates difference—opposite to the way of governance.

sentences.zh: 《傳》曰『從善如登，從惡如崩』，言善之難也。

translations.literal: The Commentary says, 'Following good is like climbing; following evil is like collapsing'—speaking of the difficulty of good.
translations.idiomatic: The Commentary says, 'Following good is like climbing; following evil is like collapsing'—such is the difficulty of doing good.

sentences.zh: 人君承奕世之基，據自然之勢，操八柄之威，甘易同之歡，無假敢於人，而忠臣挾難進之術，吐逆耳之言，其不合也，不亦宜乎！

translations.literal: A ruler inherits a foundation passed through generations, holds a position of natural advantage, wields the authority of the eight handles, delights in the ease of agreement, and need fear no one—while loyal ministers carry methods hard to advance and speak words grating to the ear; that they do not accord— is this not fitting!
translations.idiomatic: A ruler inherits a foundation passed through generations, holds a position of natural advantage, wields supreme authority, delights in the ease of agreement, and need fear no one—while loyal ministers carry methods hard to advance and speak words grating to the ear; that they do not accord—is this not fitting!

sentences.zh: 離則有釁，巧辯緣間，眩於小忠，戀於恩愛，賢愚雜錯，黜陟失敘，其所由來，情亂之也。

translations.literal: Separation then brings breach; clever argument follows the gap; dazzled by petty loyalty, attached to favor and affection, worthy and foolish are mixed, dismissal and promotion lose order—the source of this is the disorder of passion.
translations.idiomatic: Separation brings breach; clever argument follows the gap; dazzled by petty loyalty, attached to favor and affection, worthy and foolish are mixed, dismissal and promotion lose order—the source of this is the disorder of passion.

sentences.zh: 故明君寤之，求賢如飢渴，受諫而不厭，抑情損欲，以義割恩，則上無偏謬之授，下無希冀之望矣！

translations.literal: Therefore the enlightened ruler awakens to this, seeks the worthy as if hungry and thirsty, receives remonstrance without weariness, restrains passion and reduces desire, and cuts affection by righteousness—then above there are no partial or mistaken appointments, and below there are no hopes of favor!
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the enlightened ruler awakens to this, seeks the worthy as if hungry and thirsty, receives remonstrance without weariness, restrains passion and reduces desire, and cuts affection by righteousness—then above there are no partial or mistaken appointments, and below there are no hopes of favor!

translations.idiomatic: " When Sun Quan read the letter, he wept.

translations.idiomatic: 8. In winter, the tenth month, Pingwang Watchtower was renamed Tingchong Watchtower.

translations.idiomatic: The Emperor often said: "Prisons are the life-blood of the realm.

translations.idiomatic: " Whenever he decided a major case, he would go to the watchtower to hear it in person.

translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Li Kui, teacher of Marquis Wen of Wei, wrote the six chapters of the Classic of Law; Lord Shang received it and became chancellor of Qin.

translations.literal: Xiao He fixed the Han Code, adding to nine chapters; later it gradually increased to sixty chapters.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao He fixed the Han Code at nine chapters; later it gradually increased to sixty.

sentences.zh: 又有《令》三百餘篇、《決事比》九百六卷，世有增損，錯糅無常，後人各為章句，馬、鄭諸儒十有餘家，以至於魏。

translations.literal: There were also more than three hundred chapters of Ordinances and nine hundred six volumes of Precedents for Judgment; through the ages additions and deletions were made, mixed without fixed order, and later men each wrote commentaries—more than ten schools among the Ru of Ma and Zheng, down to Wei.
translations.idiomatic: There were also more than three hundred chapters of Ordinances and nine hundred six volumes of Precedents for Judgment; through the ages additions and deletions were made, mixed without fixed order, and later scholars each wrote commentaries—more than ten schools among the Ru of Ma and Zheng, down to Wei.

sentences.zh: 所當用者合二萬六千二百七十二條，七百七十三萬餘言，覽者益難。

translations.literal: What was to be applied totaled twenty-six thousand two hundred seventy-two articles and more than seven million seven hundred thirty thousand words—ever harder for readers.
translations.idiomatic: What was to be applied totaled twenty-six thousand two hundred seventy-two articles and more than seven million seven hundred thirty thousand words—ever harder for readers to master.

translations.idiomatic: The Emperor then decreed that only the Zheng school commentaries be used.

translations.idiomatic: Minister of Works Wei Gui memorialized, saying: "Penal law is what the state holds in high esteem yet private discussion holds in low contempt;

translations.literal: Prison officials are upon whom the common people hang their lives, yet those who select them hold them in low esteem.
translations.idiomatic: Prison officials are upon whom the common people hang their lives, yet those who select them hold them in low esteem.

translations.literal: The defects of royal governance may well arise from this.
translations.idiomatic: The defects of royal governance may well arise from this.

translations.literal: I request that Doctor of Law posts be established.
translations.idiomatic: I request that Doctor of Law posts be established.

translations.literal: Dong Zhao, acting as Minister over the Masses, submitted a memorial, saying: "All who possess the realm none fail to honor and esteem plain, honest, and faithful men, and deeply hate false and insincere men—because they destroy teaching and disorder governance, ruin custom and harm transformation.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Zhao, acting as Minister over the Masses, submitted a memorial, saying: "All who possess the realm honor plain, honest, and faithful men, and deeply hate false and insincere men—because they destroy teaching and disorder governance, ruin custom and harm transformation.

translations.literal: Recently Wei Feng was executed at the end of the Jian'an era, and Cao Wei was beheaded at the beginning of the Huangchu era.
translations.idiomatic: Recently Wei Feng was executed at the end of the Jian'an era, and Cao Wei was beheaded at the beginning of the Huangchu era.

sentences.zh: 伏惟前後聖詔，深疾浮偽，欲以破散邪黨，常用切齒；

translations.literal: I respectfully consider that former and latter sacred edicts deeply hated superficial falsity and wished to break up wicked cliques, often speaking with clenched teeth;
translations.idiomatic: I respectfully consider that former and latter sacred edicts deeply hated superficial falsity and wished to break up wicked cliques, often speaking with clenched teeth;

sentences.zh: 而執法之吏，皆畏其權勢，莫能糾擿，毀壞風俗，侵欲滋甚。

translations.literal: Yet the officials who enforce the law all fear their power and influence and none can investigate and expose them—custom is ruined and encroachment grows ever worse.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the officials who enforce the law all fear their power and influence and none can investigate and expose them—custom is ruined and encroachment grows ever worse.

sentences.zh: 竊見當今年少不復以學問為本，專更以交遊為業；

translations.literal: I have privately observed that the young of today no longer take learning as their foundation but devote themselves instead to socializing;
translations.idiomatic: I have privately observed that the young of today no longer take learning as their foundation but devote themselves instead to socializing;

sentences.zh: 國士不以孝悌清修為首，乃以趨勢游利為先。

translations.literal: Men of the realm do not put filial piety, brotherly duty, and pure conduct first, but rather rush after power and chase profit.
translations.idiomatic: Men of the realm do not put filial piety, brotherly duty, and pure conduct first, but rather rush after power and chase profit.

sentences.zh: 合黨連群，互相褒歎，以毀訾為罰戮，用黨譽為爵賞，附己者則歎之盈言，不附者則為作瑕釁。

translations.literal: They form cliques and link groups, praising one another; they treat slander as punishment and use clique praise as rank and reward—those who attach to them receive overflowing praise, and those who do not are given faults and breaches.
translations.idiomatic: They form cliques and link groups, praising one another; they treat slander as punishment and use clique praise as rank and reward—those who attach to them receive overflowing praise, and those who do not are given faults and breaches.

sentences.zh: 至乃相謂：『今世何憂不度邪，但求人道不勤，羅之下博耳；

translations.literal: They even say to one another: 'In this age what worry is there of not passing? One need only not be diligent in the way of men and cast a wide net—that is all;

sentences.zh: 人何患其不知己，但當吞之以藥而柔調耳。

translations.literal: What worry has a man that others do not know him? One need only swallow it with medicine and soften and adjust.'
translations.idiomatic: What worry has a man that others do not know him? One need only swallow it with medicine and soften and adjust.'

translations.idiomatic: The court forwarded Qun's objections to Zhen; Zhen held to his plan and marched anyway.

translations.idiomatic: On the day Yiwei, he reached Xuchang.

translations.idiomatic: 7. When Chancellor Zhuge Liang learned that Wei forces were approaching, he halted at Chiban in Chenggu to await them.

sentences.zh: 召李嚴使將二萬人赴漢中，表嚴子豐為江州都督，督軍典嚴後事。

translations.literal: He summoned Li Yan and had him lead twenty thousand men to Hanzhong, and memorialized to appoint Yan's son Feng as Inspector of Jiangzhou to oversee military affairs and handle Yan's rear duties.
translations.idiomatic: He summoned Li Yan with twenty thousand men to reinforce Hanzhong and memorialized to make Yan's son Feng inspector of Jiangzhou, to command troops and manage affairs in Yan's absence.

sentences.zh: 會天大雨三十餘日，棧道斷絕，太尉華歆上疏曰：「陛下以聖德當成、康之隆，願先留心於治道，以征伐為後事。

translations.literal: When Heaven sent heavy rain for more than thirty days and the plank roads were cut off, Grand Commandant Hua Xin submitted a memorial, saying: "Your Majesty by your sage virtue is equal to the flourishing age of Cheng and Kang—please first attend to the way of good government and treat campaigns as a later concern.
translations.idiomatic: Heavy rain fell for more than thirty days and the plank roads were washed out. Grand Commandant Hua Xin memorialized the throne: "Your Majesty's sage virtue matches the golden age of Kings Cheng and Kang. I beg you to fix your mind first on good government and leave campaigns for later.

sentences.zh: 為國者以民為基，民以衣食為本。

translations.literal: A state-builder takes the people as foundation; the people take food and clothing as root.
translations.idiomatic: A state rests on its people; the people rest on food and clothing.

sentences.zh: 使中國無饑寒之患，百姓無離上之心，則二賊之釁可坐而待也！

translations.literal: If within China there is no distress of hunger and cold, and the common people have no heart to abandon their sovereign, then the provocations of the two rebels can be awaited sitting down!"
translations.idiomatic: If the heartland knows neither hunger nor cold, and the people never turn from their sovereign, the two rebels' openings will come to you while you sit at ease!"

sentences.zh: 」帝報曰：「賊憑恃山川，二祖勞於前世，猶不克平，朕豈敢自多，謂必滅之哉！

translations.literal: " The Emperor replied: "The rebels rely on mountains and rivers; our two forefathers toiled in former ages yet still could not pacify them—how dare I flatter myself and say they must be destroyed!
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor answered: "The rebels hide behind mountains and rivers. Our two imperial forefathers strained themselves in earlier reigns and still could not finish them—how dare I boast that they must be destroyed!

sentences.zh: 諸將以為不一探取，無由自敝，是以觀兵以窺其釁。

translations.literal: The generals hold that without some probing advance there is no way to wear them down by themselves—that is why we parade the army to spy out their provocations.
translations.idiomatic: My generals argue that without some probing thrust the enemy will never wear themselves down—so we parade the army to test where they are vulnerable.

sentences.zh: 若天時未至，周武還師，乃前事之鑒，朕敬不忘所戒。

translations.literal: If the season of Heaven has not come, King Wu of Zhou withdrew his army—that is the lesson of former events; I respectfully do not forget the warning."
translations.idiomatic: If Heaven's season has not arrived, recall how King Wu of Zhou turned his army back—that is the lesson of history, and I do not forget the warning."

sentences.zh: 少府楊阜上疏曰：「昔武王白魚入舟，君臣變色，動得吉瑞，猶尚憂懼，況有災異而不戰竦者哉！

translations.literal: Minor Treasurer Yang Fu submitted a memorial, saying: "Formerly when King Wu's white fish entered the boat, lord and ministers changed color; though he received auspicious omens in his movements, he still was anxious and fearful—how much more when there are calamities and portents and one does not shudder at war!
translations.idiomatic: Minor Treasurer Yang Fu memorialized the throne: "When King Wu's white fish leapt into the boat, lord and ministers turned pale. Though every omen he met was auspicious, he still feared what might come—how much more should we tremble at war when Heaven sends calamity after calamity!

sentences.zh: 今吳、蜀未平，而天屢降變，諸軍始進，便有天雨之患，稽閡山險，已積日矣。

translations.literal: Now Wu and Shu are not yet pacified, yet Heaven repeatedly sends abnormal events; the armies have barely set out when the affliction of rain came; blocked by mountain passes, days have already piled up.
translations.idiomatic: Wu and Shu are still unconquered, yet Heaven keeps sending portents. The armies had barely marched when the rains struck; hemmed in by mountain passes, they have been stalled for days on end.

sentences.zh: 轉運之勞，擔負之苦，所費已多，若有不斷，必違本圖。

translations.literal: The toil of transport, the hardship of carrying loads—the expense is already great; if there is no decisive break, our fundamental plan will surely be betrayed.
translations.idiomatic: The labor of convoys and porters has already cost dearly. Without a clean decision now, the original design of the campaign will be lost.

sentences.zh: 《傳》曰：『見可而進，知難而退，軍之善政也。

translations.literal: The Documents say: 'See what is feasible and advance; know what is hard and withdraw—that is good policy in war.'
translations.idiomatic: The Documents say: 'Advance when you see your opening; withdraw when you know the difficulty—that is sound military policy.'

sentences.zh: 』徒使六軍困於山谷之間，進無所略，退又不得，非王兵之道也。

translations.literal: ' To leave the Six Armies trapped between mountain valleys, advancing with nothing to seize and retreating with no way out—that is not the way of a royal army."
translations.idiomatic: ' To leave the Six Armies penned in the mountains—nothing to take if they advance, no road if they retreat—is not the way of a royal army."

sentences.zh: 散騎常侍王肅王上疏曰：「前志有之：『千里饋糧，士有饑色，樵蘇後爨，師不宿飽，』此謂平塗之行軍者也；

translations.literal: Attendant Cavalier Wang Su submitted a memorial, saying: "Former records have it: 'Grain supplied from a thousand li, and the soldiers wear hunger on their faces; woodcutters gather fuel only after others have cooked, and the army is never well fed overnight'—this describes an army marching on level ground;
translations.idiomatic: Attendant Cavalier Wang Su memorialized the throne: "The old books say, 'Supply grain from a thousand li away and your soldiers go hungry; woodcutters gather fuel only after the cooks have finished, and the army never sleeps on a full belly'—and that is for armies marching on level roads.

sentences.zh: 又況於深入阻險，鑿路而前，則其為勞必相百也。

translations.literal: How much more when penetrating deep into obstructed terrain and hewing a path forward—the labor must be multiplied a hundredfold.
translations.idiomatic: How much worse when you drive deep into broken country and cut your way forward—the strain must be a hundred times greater.

sentences.zh: 今又加之以霖雨，山板峻滑，眾迫而不展，糧遠而難繼，實行軍者之大忌也。

translations.literal: Now added to this is incessant rain; mountain planks are steep and slippery; the mass is pressed and cannot deploy; provisions are distant and hard to relay—this is truly a great chief taboo for an army on the march.
translations.idiomatic: Add unending rain, planks slick on the cliffs, troops packed too tight to maneuver, and grain lines stretched too far to sustain—this is the gravest taboo for any army on the march.

sentences.zh: 聞曹真發已逾月而行裁半谷，治道功夫，戰士悉作。

translations.literal: I hear that since Cao Zhen set out more than a month has passed, yet the march has covered barely half a valley; road work and labor—every fighting man is at it.
translations.idiomatic: I hear Cao Zhen has been on the road more than a month and has barely crossed half a valley—every fighting man is still building the road.

sentences.zh: 是賊偏得以逸待勞，乃兵家之所憚也。

translations.literal: Thus the rebels on their part get to await the weary with rested troops—that is what military families dread.
translations.idiomatic: That lets the enemy wait fresh while our men wear themselves out—the very thing every strategist dreads.

sentences.zh: 言之前代，則武王伐紂，出關而復還；

translations.literal: Speaking of earlier ages, King Wu attacked Zhou, passed out of the Pass and then returned;
translations.idiomatic: Look to antiquity: King Wu marched against Zhou, passed out of the Pass, and turned back;

sentences.zh: 論之近事，則武、文征權，臨江而不濟。

translations.literal: Speaking of recent events, Emperor Wu and Emperor Wen campaigned against Quan, came to the river and did not cross.
translations.idiomatic: Look to recent times: Emperors Wu and Wen campaigned against Sun Quan, reached the river, and did not cross.

sentences.zh: 豈非所謂順天知時，通於權變者哉！

translations.literal: Is this not what is called according with Heaven, knowing the season, and mastering flexible adaptation!
translations.idiomatic: Is that not what it means to follow Heaven, read the season, and know when to bend?

sentences.zh: 兆民知上聖以水雨艱劇之故，休而息之，後日有釁，乘而用之，則所謂悅以犯難，民忘其死者矣。

translations.literal: Let the myriad people know that the supreme sage, because of the hardship of rain and flood, rests and gives them repose; when later there is provocation, seize it and use it—then what is called 'delighted to face hardship, the people forget death' will be achieved."
translations.idiomatic: Let the people see that their sage ruler, because rain and flood have made the road impossible, gives them rest. When the next opening comes, seize it—and then you will have what the books call men who delight in hardship and forget death."

sentences.zh: 」肅，朗之子也。

translations.literal: " Su was the son of Lang.
translations.idiomatic: Su was the son of Wang Lang.

sentences.zh: 九月，詔曹真等班師。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, an edict ordered Cao Zhen and the others to withdraw the army.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, an edict recalled Cao Zhen and his army.

sentences.zh: 8冬，十月，乙卯，帝還洛陽。

translations.literal: 8. In winter, the tenth month, on the day Yimao, the Emperor returned to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: 8. In winter, the tenth month, on the day Yimao, the Emperor returned to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 時左僕射徐宣總統留事，帝還，主者奏呈文書。

translations.literal: At the time Left Vice Director Xu Xuan was in overall charge of affairs left behind; when the Emperor returned, the attending clerks presented memorials and documents.
translations.idiomatic: Left Vice Director Xu Xuan had been left in charge of the capital. When the Emperor returned, the clerks brought forward the accumulated papers.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「吾省與僕射省何異！

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "What difference is there between my review and the Vice Director's review!
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "What difference is there between my review and the Vice Director's?

sentences.zh: 」竟不視。

translations.literal: " In the end he did not look at them.
translations.idiomatic: " In the end he did not look at them.

sentences.zh: 9十二月，〔辛未〕<ref>〔辛未〕據章注及《魏志．明帝紀》補。

translations.literal: 9. In the twelfth month, [Xinwei]<ref>[Xinwei] supplied according to Zhang's commentary and the Annals of Mingdi in the Records of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: 9. In the twelfth month, on the day Xinwei<ref>Supplied according to Zhang's commentary and the Annals of Mingdi in the Records of Wei.

sentences.zh: </ref>，改葬文昭皇后于朝陽陵。

translations.literal: </ref>, Empress Wen Zhao was reburied at Chaoyang Tomb.
translations.idiomatic: [End editorial note.] Empress Wen Zhao was reburied at Chaoyang Tomb.

sentences.zh: 10吳主揚聲欲至合肥，征東將軍滿寵表召兗、豫諸軍皆集，吳尋退還，詔罷其兵。

translations.literal: 10. The King of Wu gave out that he meant to reach Hefei; General Who Subdues the East Man Chong memorialized to summon all armies of Yan and Yu to assemble; Wu soon withdrew, and an edict dismissed those troops.
translations.idiomatic: 10. Sun Quan gave out that he meant to march on Hefei. Man Chong, General Who Subdues the East, memorialized to muster the armies of Yan and Yu. Wu soon withdrew, and an edict stood the troops down.

sentences.zh: 寵以為：「今賊大舉而還，非本意也，此必欲偽退以罷吾兵，而倒還乘虛，掩不備也。

translations.literal: Chong argued: "Now the rebels have come in force and are withdrawing—this is not their true intent; they surely mean to feign withdrawal to get our troops stood down, then turn back and strike at an empty moment when we are unprepared.
translations.idiomatic: Chong argued: "The enemy came in force and is withdrawing—that is not their real intent. They mean to feign retreat, get our troops dismissed, then wheel about and strike where we are unprepared.

sentences.zh: 」表不罷兵，後十餘日，吳果更來。

translations.literal: " He memorialized not to dismiss the troops; more than ten days later Wu indeed came again.
translations.idiomatic: " He memorialized against standing the troops down. More than ten days later Wu returned as he had predicted.

sentences.zh: 到合肥城，不克而還。

translations.literal: They reached Hefei city but could not take it and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: They reached Hefei but could not take it and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 11漢丞相亮以蔣琬為長史。

translations.literal: 11. Han Chancellor Liang made Jiang Wan Chief Clerk.
translations.idiomatic: 11. Chancellor Zhuge Liang appointed Jiang Wan chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 亮數外出，琬常足食兵，以相供給。

translations.literal: When Liang went out on campaign many times, Wan regularly supplied full provisions for the troops to meet each other's needs.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Liang took the field, Wan kept the army fed and the supply lines running.

sentences.zh: 亮每言：「公琰託志忠雅，當與吾共贊王業者也。

translations.literal: Liang often said: "Gongyan has entrusted his will to loyalty and refinement—he should work with me to support the royal enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: Liang often said, "Gongyan's heart is loyal and steady. He is the man to help me sustain the royal enterprise.

sentences.zh: 12青州人隱蕃逃奔入吳，上書於吳主曰：「臣聞紂為無道，微子先出；

translations.literal: 12. Yin Fan of Qing Province fled and defected to Wu, submitting a memorial to the King of Wu, saying: "I have heard that when Zhou was without the Way, Weizi departed first;
translations.idiomatic: 12. Yin Fan of Qing Province fled to Wu and memorialized Sun Quan: "I have heard that when Zhou lost the Way, Weizi left first;

sentences.zh: 高祖寬明，陳平先入。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu was broad and enlightened, and Chen Ping entered first.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu was magnanimous and clear-sighted, and Chen Ping came over first.

sentences.zh: 臣年二十二，委棄封域，歸命有道，賴蒙天靈，得自全致。

translations.literal: I am twenty-two years old; I abandoned my fief and submitted to one who possesses the Way; trusting in Heaven's numinous favor, I have preserved myself whole.
translations.idiomatic: I am twenty-two. I abandoned my domain and submitted to a ruler who holds the Way. By Heaven's grace I have come through whole.

sentences.zh: 臣至止有日，而主者同之降人，未見精別，使臣微言妙旨不得上達，於邑三歎，曷惟其已！

translations.literal: I have been here only a few days, yet those in charge lump me with other surrenderers and fail to distinguish finely—so my subtle words and fine meanings cannot reach the top; thrice I sigh in distress—how can this be ended!
translations.idiomatic: I have been here only a few days, yet the officials treat me like any other defector and never look closely enough for my finer points to reach you. Three times I have sighed in frustration—when will it end!

sentences.zh: 謹詣闕拜章，乞蒙引見。

translations.literal: I respectfully come to the palace gate to present this memorial, begging to be granted an audience.
translations.idiomatic: I respectfully come to the palace gate with this memorial and beg for an audience.

sentences.zh: 」吳主即召入，蕃進謝，答問及陳時務，甚有辭觀。

translations.literal: " The King of Wu immediately summoned him in; Fan entered to give thanks, answered questions, and set forth current affairs—very fine in language and bearing.
translations.idiomatic: " Sun Quan summoned him at once. Fan entered to give thanks, answered questions, and spoke on current affairs with impressive eloquence and bearing.

sentences.zh: 侍中右領軍胡綜侍坐，吳主問：「何如？

translations.literal: Attendant-in-Ordinary and Right Leader of the Guards Hu Zong sat in attendance; the King of Wu asked: "What do you think?
translations.idiomatic: Attendant-in-Ordinary and Right Leader of the Guards Hu Zong sat with him. Sun Quan asked, "What do you think?

sentences.zh: 」綜對曰：「蕃上書大語有似東方朔，巧捷詭辯有似檷衡，而才皆不及。

translations.literal: " Zong replied: "In Fan's memorial the grand words resemble Dongfang Shuo; the clever agility and devious debate resemble Mi Heng—but in talent he falls short of both.
translations.idiomatic: " Zong answered, "In his memorial Fan's grand phrases recall Dongfang Shuo, and his quick, devious wit recalls Mi Heng—but in talent he falls short of both.

sentences.zh: 」吳主又問：「可堪何官？

translations.literal: " The King of Wu asked again: "What office can he fill?
translations.idiomatic: " Sun Quan asked again, "What office could he fill?

sentences.zh: 」綜對曰：「未可以治民，且試都輦小職。

translations.literal: " Zong replied: "He is not yet fit to govern the people; let him for now be tried in a minor metropolitan post.
translations.idiomatic: " Zong answered, "He is not yet fit to govern the people. Try him first in some minor post at court.

sentences.zh: 」吳主以蕃盛語刑獄，用為廷尉監。

translations.literal: " The King of Wu, because Fan spoke eloquently on criminal cases, appointed him Supervisor of the Court of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: " Because Fan spoke impressively on criminal matters, Sun Quan made him supervisor of the Court of Justice.

sentences.zh: 左將軍朱據、廷尉郝普數稱蕃有王佐之才，普尤與之親善，常怨嘆其屈。

translations.literal: Left General Zhu Ju and Court of Justice Director Hao Pu repeatedly praised Fan as having talent to assist a king; Pu was especially close to him and often lamented that he was passed over.
translations.idiomatic: Left General Zhu Ju and Court of Justice Director Hao Pu repeatedly praised Fan as a man with king-making talent. Pu was especially close to him and often lamented that his gifts were wasted.

sentences.zh: 於是蕃門車馬雲集，賓客盈堂，自衛將軍全琮等皆傾心接待；

translations.literal: Thereupon at Fan's gate chariots and horses gathered like clouds and guests filled the hall; from General of the Guard Quan Cong on down, all received him with devoted hospitality;
translations.idiomatic: Soon chariots and horses crowded Fan's gate and guests filled his hall. From General of the Guard Quan Cong on down, men vied to receive him.

sentences.zh: 惟羊衜及宣詔郎豫章楊迪拒絕不與通。

translations.literal: only Yang Tong and Palace Edict Officer Yang Di of Yuzhang refused contact with him.
translations.idiomatic: Only Yang Tong and Palace Edict Officer Yang Di of Yuzhang refused to have anything to do with him.

sentences.zh: 潘濬子翥，亦與蕃周旋，饋餉之。

translations.literal: Pan Jun's son Xu also kept company with Fan and sent him provisions.
translations.idiomatic: Pan Jun's son Xu also kept company with Fan and sent him gifts of food.

sentences.zh: 濬聞，大怒，疏責翥曰：「吾受國厚恩，志報以命，爾輩在都，當念恭順，親賢慕善。

translations.literal: Jun heard of this and flew into a rage; in a memorial he rebuked Xu, saying: "I have received the state's deep favor and intend to repay it with my life; you who are in the capital should think on respectful obedience and be close to the worthy while admiring goodness.
translations.idiomatic: Jun heard of it and was furious. In a memorial he rebuked Xu: "I owe the state a deep debt and mean to repay it with my life. You who are in the capital should be respectful, keep company with the worthy, and admire what is good.

sentences.zh: 何故與降虜交，以糧餉之！

translations.literal: Why do you keep company with a surrendered captive and send him grain!
translations.idiomatic: Why do you keep company with a surrendered captive and feed him!

sentences.zh: 在遠聞此，心震面熱，惆悵累旬。

translations.literal: Hearing this from afar, my heart trembles and my face burns; I have been distressed for many days.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing this from afar, my heart trembles and my face burns. I have brooded over it for days on end.

sentences.zh: 疏到，急就往使受杖一百，促責所餉！

translations.literal: When this memorial arrives, go at once and have the bearer beaten a hundred strokes, and urgently demand back what was sent!"
translations.idiomatic: When this memorial arrives, go at once and have the bearer beaten a hundred strokes, and demand back everything you sent!"

sentences.zh: 」當時人咸怪之。

translations.literal: " At the time people all found it strange.
translations.idiomatic: " People at the time all thought it strange.

sentences.zh: 頃之，蕃謀作亂於吳，事覺，亡走，捕得，伏誅。

translations.literal: Before long Fan plotted rebellion in Wu; the affair was discovered; he fled but was captured and executed.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Fan plotted rebellion in Wu. The plot was discovered; he fled, was captured, and executed.

sentences.zh: 吳主切責郝普，普惶懼，自殺。

translations.literal: The King of Wu sharply rebuked Hao Pu; Pu was terrified and killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan sharply rebuked Hao Pu. Terrified, Pu killed himself.

sentences.zh: 朱據禁止，歷時乃解。

translations.literal: Zhu Ju was placed under house arrest; only after a full year was he released.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Ju was placed under house arrest and was not released until a full year had passed.

sentences.zh: 13武陵五溪蠻夷叛吳，吳主以南土清定，召交州剌史呂岱還屯長沙漚口。

translations.literal: 13. The barbarians of the Five Streams in Wuling rebelled against Wu; the King of Wu, because the southern lands were pacified, recalled Inspector of Jiaozhou Lü Dai to encamp at Oukou in Changsha.
translations.idiomatic: 13. The tribal peoples of the Five Streams in Wuling rebelled against Wu. Because the south was now quiet, Sun Quan recalled Lü Dai, inspector of Jiaozhou, to encamp at Oukou in Changsha.
